title.zh: 卷四十八 列傳第十八 向雄 段灼 閻纘
title.en: Volume 48 Biographies 18: Xiang Xiong; Duan Zhuo; Yan Zuan
title.raw: 卷四十八 列傳第十八 向雄 段灼 閻纘 Volume 48 Biographies 18: Xiang Xiong; Duan Zhuo; Yan Zuan

sentences.zh: 向雄 段灼 閻纘

translations.literal: Xiang Xiong; Duan Zhuo; Yan Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Xiang Xiong, Duan Zhuo, and Yan Zuan.

sentences.zh: 向雄，字茂伯，河內山陽人也。

translations.literal: Xiang Xiong, courtesy Maobo, was a man of Shanyang in Hanoi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xiong, courtesy name Maobo, came from Shanyang in Hanoi.

sentences.zh: 父韶，彭城太守。

translations.literal: His father Xiang Shao was Grand Administrator of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Xiang Shao, had served as governor of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 雄初仕郡為主簿，事太守王經。

translations.literal: At first Xiong served the commandery as chief clerk and attended Grand Administrator Wang Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xiong began his career as chief clerk of the commandery under Prefect Wang Jing.

sentences.zh: 及經之死也，雄哭之盡哀，市人咸為之悲。

translations.literal: When it came to Jing's death, Xiong wept for him with complete grief; market people all for it felt sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jing was put to death, Xiang Xiong mourned him bitterly, and the crowds at the execution ground wept with him.

sentences.zh: 後太守劉毅嘗以非罪笞雄，及吳奮代毅為太守，又以少譴系雄於獄。

translations.literal: Later Grand Administrator Liu Yi once for no real crime flogged Xiong; when Wu Fen replaced Yi as grand administrator, again for a slight fault he bound Xiong in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Prefect Liu Yi had him flogged without real cause; when Wu Fen succeeded Liu Yi, he jailed Xiang Xiong over a minor reprimand.

sentences.zh: 司隸鐘會於獄中辟雄為都官從事，會死無人殯斂，雄迎喪而葬之。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Governor Zhong Hui from within prison summoned Xiong as clerk for capital affairs; when Hui died none laid him out, and Xiong received the corpse and buried it.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan Commissioner Zhong Hui recruited him from jail as an aide in judicial affairs; after Zhong Hui died with no one to lay him out, Xiang Xiong claimed the body and gave him burial.

sentences.zh: 文帝召雄而責之曰：「往者王經之死，卿哭王經於東市，我不問也。

translations.literal: King Wen summoned Xiong and reproached him, saying: When formerly Wang Jing died, you wept for Wang Jing at the eastern market; I did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen summoned Xiang Xiong and rebuked him: When Wang Jing died, you mourned him publicly at the eastern market; I let that pass.

sentences.zh: 今鐘會躬為叛逆，又輒收葬，若復相容，其如王法何！

translations.literal: Now Zhong Hui personally was a rebel; again you presumptuously gathered and buried him. If again we tolerate one another, what of royal law!
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui turned traitor with his own hands, yet you took it on yourself to bury him. If such behavior keeps getting a pass, what becomes of the law?

sentences.zh: 」雄曰：「昔者先王掩骼埋胔，仁流朽骨，當時豈先卜其功罪而後葬之哉！

translations.literal: Xiong said: Of old the former kings covered bones and buried flesh left exposed; benevolence reached rotten bones. In that age did they first divine merit and guilt and afterward bury them!
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xiong replied: The kings of old gathered exposed bones and buried the dead; their kindness extended even to decayed remains. Did they first weigh each person's guilt or merit before granting burial?

sentences.zh: 今王誅既加，於法已備。

translations.literal: Now kingly punishment already has been applied; in law it is already complete.
translations.idiomatic: Royal justice has already been carried out; the sentence under law is finished.

sentences.zh: 雄感義收葬，教亦無闕。

translations.literal: Xiong, moved by duty, gathered and buried; in instruction also there is no lack.
translations.idiomatic: I buried him out of a sense of moral duty, and that breaks no principle of moral teaching.

sentences.zh: 法立於上，教弘於下，何必使雄違生背死以立于時！

translations.literal: Law is set above; instruction spreads below—why must one make Xiong violate the living and turn against the dead so as to stand in the age!
translations.idiomatic: Law comes from above and moral teaching spreads below; why must you force me to dishonor the living and betray the dead just to cut a figure in this world?

sentences.zh: 殿下仇枯骨而捐之中野，為將來仁賢之資，不亦惜乎！

translations.literal: Your Highness hates dry bones and casts them away in the open wild—material for later humane and worthy men—is it not regrettable!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Highness leaves dried bones as enemies and abandons them in the wilderness, you supply posterity's humane and worthy men with a sad precedent—is that not a pity?

sentences.zh: 」帝甚悅，與談宴而遣之。

translations.literal: The king greatly delighted; with him he conversed at banquet and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: The king was greatly pleased, talked with him over a feast, and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 累遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: By stages he was transferred to Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to become a gentleman attendant at the palace Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 時吳奮、劉毅俱為侍中，同在門下，雄初不交言。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Fen and Liu Yi both were palace attendants, together under the gate; at first Xiong did not exchange words.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fen and Liu Yi were both palace attendants serving together at court, yet Xiang Xiong still refused to speak to them.

sentences.zh: 武帝聞之，敕雄令復君臣之好。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu heard of it and ordered Xiong to restore lord-minister cordiality.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu learned of this, he ordered Xiang Xiong to mend relations with his former superiors.

sentences.zh: 雄不得已，乃詣毅，再拜曰：「向被詔命，君臣義絕，如何？

translations.literal: Xiong having no choice, then went to Yi, twice bowed and said: Just now having received an edict-order, lord-minister righteousness is cut off—how shall it be?
translations.idiomatic: Reluctantly Xiang Xiong went to Liu Yi, bowed twice, and said: I have just been commanded to restore cordiality, but the moral bond between lord and minister is already broken—what am I to do?

sentences.zh: 」於是即去。

translations.literal: Thereupon at once he departed.
translations.idiomatic: With that he turned and left.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而大怒，問雄曰：「我令卿復君臣之好，何以故絕？

translations.literal: The emperor heard and greatly raged; he asked Xiong: I ordered you to restore lord-minister cordiality—why therefore cut it off?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and demanded: I told you to patch things up with your former chief—why did you sever ties instead?

sentences.zh: 」雄曰：「古之君子進人以禮，退人以禮；

translations.literal: Xiong said: The gentlemen of antiquity advanced others by ritual and dismissed others by ritual;
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xiong answered: Men of virtue in antiquity brought others forward courteously and parted from them courteously;

sentences.zh: 今之進人若加諸膝，退人若墜諸川。

translations.literal: those of today who advance others are as placing them on one's knees; those who dismiss others are as dropping them into streams.
translations.idiomatic: today favorites are lifted onto one's lap, and cast-offs are hurled into the ditch.

sentences.zh: 劉河內於臣不為戎首，亦已幸甚，安復為君臣之好！

translations.literal: Liu of Hanoi toward your servant did not act as war-leader—that already is very fortunate; how again lord-minister cordiality!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi did not make himself my mortal enemy as governor of Hanoi; I already count that lucky. How could we pretend to warm lord-and-minister feelings?

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，累遷秦州刺史，假赤幢、曲蓋、鼓吹，賜錢二十萬。

translations.literal: In the Taishi years, by stages he was transferred to governor of Qinzhou; he was lent crimson canopy, curved umbrella, and drum-and-pipe band; two hundred thousand cash were granted.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taishi era he advanced to governor of Qin Province, was granted the crimson banner, curved ceremonial canopy, and military musicians, and received a gift of two hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 咸甯初，入為御史中丞，遷侍中，又出為征虜將軍。

translations.literal: At the start of Xianning, he entered as imperial secretary vice-director; was transferred to palace attendant; again went out as general who conquers barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianning he was recalled to serve as vice director of the imperial secretariat, promoted to palace attendant, then sent out again as general for barbarian suppression.

sentences.zh: 太康初，為河南尹，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: At the start of Taikang, he became Intendant of Henan; a rank of marquis within the passes was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taikang he became prefect of the Henan metropolitan district and was ennobled as a secondary marquis.

sentences.zh: 齊王攸將歸籓，雄諫曰：「陛下子弟雖多，然有名望者少。

translations.literal: Prince Qi Sima You was about to return to his fief; Xiong remonstrated: Your Majesty's sons and younger brothers though many, yet those with fame and repute are few.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Qi, Sima You, was ordered back to his princedom, Xiang Xiong urged against it: You have many imperial clansmen, but few who truly command respect.

sentences.zh: 齊王臥在京邑，所益實深，不可不思。

translations.literal: Prince Qi lies at the capital seat; the benefit thereby is truly deep—not possible not to ponder.
translations.idiomatic: Keeping Prince Qi at the capital does profound good for the realm; you must weigh this carefully.

sentences.zh: 」帝不納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 雄固諫忤旨，起而徑出，遂以憤卒。

translations.literal: Xiong stubbornly remonstrated and offended intent; he rose and went straight out; thereby in resentment he died.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xiong pressed his advice until he angered the throne, then rose and walked straight out of court; he died soon afterward, consumed by indignation.

sentences.zh: 弟匡，惠帝世為護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Younger brother Kuang, in Emperor Hui's age was general who guards the army.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xiang Kuang became protector-general under Emperor Hui.

sentences.zh: 段灼，字休然，敦煌人也。

translations.literal: Duan Zhuo, courtesy Xiuran, was a man of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Zhuo, courtesy name Xiuran, was a native of Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 世為西土著姓，果直有才辯。

translations.literal: For generations they were a great surname of the western lands; he was frank and upright and had talent in disputation.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long been a powerful clan of the northwest; he was blunt, upright, and a gifted debater.

sentences.zh: 少仕州郡，稍遷鄧艾鎮西司馬，從艾破蜀有功，封關內侯，累遷議郎。

translations.literal: In youth he served prefectures and commanderies; gradually was promoted Deng Ai's west-guarding army marshal; following Ai he broke Shu with merit; enfeoffed marquis within the passes; by stages transferred to gentleman consultant.
translations.idiomatic: He entered local administration young, rose to become Deng Ai's chief of staff on the western front, earned distinction in the conquest of Shu, was made a secondary marquis, and eventually reached the post of advisory gentleman.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，灼上疏追理艾曰：

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Zhuo submitted a memorial pursuing judgment for Ai, saying:
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu took the throne, Duan Zhuo submitted a memorial arguing for Deng Ai's rehabilitation:

sentences.zh: 故征西將軍鄧艾，心懷至忠，而荷反逆之名；

translations.literal: The former general who conquered the west Deng Ai, in heart cherished utmost loyalty, yet bore the name of rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: The late Deng Ai, former general of the western expedition, was utterly loyal at heart yet was branded a traitor;

sentences.zh: 平定巴、蜀，而受三族之誅，臣竊悼之。

translations.literal: he pacified Ba and Shu, yet received execution of three clans; your servant secretly mourns him.
translations.idiomatic: he conquered Ba and Shu for the court, then suffered the extirpation of three generations of his kin—I mourn him in private.

sentences.zh: 惜哉，言艾之反也！

translations.literal: Alas, they speak of Ai's rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: How regrettable that people still call Deng Ai a rebel!

sentences.zh: 以艾性剛急，矜功伐善，而不能協同朋類，輕犯雅俗，失君子之心，故莫肯理之。

translations.literal: Because Ai's nature was rigid and hasty, he boasted of merit and vaunted goodness, yet could not cooperate with peers and companions; lightly he offended refined custom—lost gentlemen's hearts—therefore none were willing to straighten his case.
translations.idiomatic: Because Deng Ai was blunt and impatient, crowed over his deeds and vaunted his superiority, refused to get along with colleagues, and casually offended respectable opinion, he forfeited the sympathy of good men—so nobody would plead his innocence.

sentences.zh: 臣敢昧死言艾所以不反之狀。

translations.literal: Your servant dares, blinding death, to speak the forms by which Ai therefore did not rebel.
translations.idiomatic: I risk execution to explain why Deng Ai could not have been plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 艾本屯田掌犢人，宣皇帝拔之于農吏之中，顯之於宰府之職。

translations.literal: Ai originally was a man who managed oxen for agricultural colonies; Emperor Xuan pulled him from among farming clerks and displayed him in steward-office posts.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai began as a lowly clerk overseeing ox teams on the military farms; Emperor Xuan pulled him from that obscurity and advanced him to responsible posts at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 處內外之官，據文武之任，所在輒有名績，固足以明宣皇帝之知人矣。

translations.literal: He occupied inner and outer offices, grasped civil and martial duties; wherever posted, always there were famed deeds—solidly sufficient to clarify Emperor Xuan's knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: Whether at court or in the field, in civil or military roles, he produced a distinguished record everywhere he served—clear proof that Emperor Xuan knew how to spot talent.

sentences.zh: 會值洮西之役，官兵失利，刺史王經困於圍城之中。

translations.literal: It happened to meet the Tao-west campaign; court troops suffered defeat; Inspector Wang Jing was trapped within besieged walls.
translations.idiomatic: Then came the disaster on the Tao River: imperial forces were routed and Inspector Wang Jing was trapped inside a siege.

sentences.zh: 當爾之時，二州危懼，隴右懍懍，幾非國家之有也。

translations.literal: At that moment the two provinces were in peril and fear; Longyou trembled—it was almost not the state's possession.
translations.idiomatic: Both provinces were panic-stricken; the Longyou frontier shook; the region nearly ceased to belong to the state.

sentences.zh: 先帝以為深憂重慮，思惟可以安邊殺敵莫賢于艾，故授之以兵馬，解狄道之圍。

translations.literal: The late emperor took it as deep worry and heavy concern; reflecting that none who could pacify the border and kill the enemy surpassed Ai, therefore he entrusted him with troops and horses and relieved Didao's siege.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor worried deeply and concluded that no one could secure the frontier and strike the enemy better than Deng Ai, so he gave him an army and lifted the siege of Didao.

sentences.zh: 圍解，留屯上邽。

translations.literal: The siege relieved, he remained garrisoned at Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: After the siege broke, Deng Ai stayed on to garrison Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 承官軍大敗之後，士卒破膽，將吏無氣，倉庫空虛，器械殫盡。

translations.literal: Receiving after court army great defeat, troops broke liver-gall; commanders and clerks without breath; granaries empty and void; weapons exhausted to end.
translations.idiomatic: Coming right after a shattering defeat, the soldiers were demoralized, officers had no fight left, stores stood empty, and equipment was gone.

sentences.zh: 艾欲積穀強兵，以待有事。

translations.literal: Ai wished to pile grain and strengthen troops, to await there being affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai wanted to stockpile grain and rebuild the army against whatever came next.

sentences.zh: 是歲少雨，又為區種之法，手執耒耜，率先將士，所統萬數，而身不離僕虜之勞，親執士卒之役。

translations.literal: That year rain was scant; again he practiced pit-field method; hand grasping plough-hoe, he led ahead generals and soldiers; those commanded numbered in myriads, yet his person did not depart labor of servants and captives—personally performed soldiers' corvee.
translations.idiomatic: Rain was scarce that year, so he introduced pit planting, took hoe and plough in his own hands, and led tens of thousands of troops by example, sharing the dirty work of common soldiers and bondsmen.

sentences.zh: 故落門、段谷之戰，能以少擊多，摧破強賊，斬首萬計。

translations.literal: Therefore at Luomen and at Duangu battles, able with few to strike many, he crushed strong bandits; beheaded counted in myriads.
translations.idiomatic: That is why at Luomen and Duangu he could attack greatly superior forces, shatter powerful enemies, and pile up tens of thousands of counted heads.

sentences.zh: 遂委艾以廟勝成圖，指授長策。

translations.literal: Thereupon they entrusted Ai with temple-victory completed plans; pointed and handed long strategies.
translations.idiomatic: The court then entrusted him with the grand strategy drawn up in council and gave him wide discretionary powers.

sentences.zh: 艾受命忘身，龍驤麟振，前無堅敵。

translations.literal: Ai received mandate forgetting self; dragon-soaring, unicorn-shaking—before him no firm foe.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai obeyed orders as if his life meant nothing; he swept forward like a charging dragon or bounding unicorn and met no foe who could stand firm.

sentences.zh: 蜀地阻險，山高穀深，而艾步乘不滿二萬，束馬懸車，自投死地，勇氣陵雲，將士乘勢，故能使劉禪震怖，君臣面縛。

translations.literal: Shu terrain was barrier-steep; mountains high, valleys deep; yet Ai's foot and horse did not fill twenty thousand; he bundled horses and suspended carts, himself threw into dead ground; courage overtopped clouds; generals and soldiers rode momentum—therefore able to make Liu Shan tremble in terror; lord and ministers with faces bound.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was a maze of precipices and deep defiles, yet Deng Ai took fewer than twenty thousand foot and horse, packed horses and hoisted carts over cliffs, and marched into what looked like certain death; courage pierced the clouds, and his men rode that surge until Liu Shan shook with terror and Shu rulers came out bound at their own bidding.

sentences.zh: 軍不逾時，而巴、蜀蕩定，此艾固足以彰先帝之善任矣。

translations.literal: The army not exceeding season, yet Ba and Shu were swept settled—this Ai solidly was sufficient to manifest the late emperor's good employment of men.
translations.idiomatic: In short order Ba and Shu were pacified—clear proof that the late emperor had chosen the right man.

sentences.zh: 艾功名已成，亦當書之竹帛，傳祚萬世。

translations.literal: Ai's merit and fame already completed—also ought be written on bamboo and silk; fortune transmitted myriad generations.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai had already secured enduring fame; his deeds belonged on bamboo slips and silk for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 七十老公，復何所求哉！

translations.literal: A seventy-year-old man—again what does he seek!
translations.idiomatic: What more could a man of seventy possibly want?

sentences.zh: 艾以禪初降，遠郡未附，矯令承制，權安社稷。

translations.literal: Ai, because Shan had first surrendered, distant commanderies not yet attached, falsely ordered acting under mandate—temporarily to settle altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Because Liu Shan had just surrendered and outlying districts had not yet submitted, Deng Ai issued orders in the emperor's name as an emergency measure to stabilize the state.

sentences.zh: 雖違常科，有合古義，原心定罪，事可詳論。

translations.literal: Though it violated constant statutes, it matched ancient meaning; tracing the heart to fix guilt—the affair permits detailed discussion.
translations.idiomatic: That bent the usual rules but matched ancient precedent; his motives deserve careful weighing before we call it a crime.

sentences.zh: 故鎮西將軍鐘會，有吞天下之心，恐艾威名，知必不同，因其疑似，構成其事。

translations.literal: Therefore General Who Guards the West Zhong Hui had a heart to swallow the world; he feared Ai's martial name; knew they surely would not agree—thereupon using his doubtful likeness, he fabricated the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui, general of the western garrison, dreamed of seizing the empire; he feared Deng Ai's prestige and knew they could never cooperate, so he seized on ambiguous evidence and framed him.

sentences.zh: 艾被詔書，即遣強兵，束身就縛，不敢顧望。

translations.literal: Ai received the edict document; at once he sent strong troops; bound body and submitted to bonds—dared not look back.
translations.idiomatic: When the summons reached him, Deng Ai dismissed his heavy guard, let himself be tied, and never hesitated or looked back.

sentences.zh: 誠自知奉見先帝，必無當死之理也。

translations.literal: Truly he himself knew that presenting himself to see the late emperor, surely there was no principle warranting death.
translations.idiomatic: He believed that once he stood before the late emperor he could not possibly deserve death.

sentences.zh: 會受誅之後，艾參佐官屬、部曲將吏，愚戇相聚，自共追艾，破壞檻車，解其囚執。

translations.literal: After Hui received execution, Ai's staff clerks and commanders, foolish and blunt gathered together; themselves together pursued Ai; broke prison cart; released his prisoner bonds.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhong Hui was executed, Deng Ai's staff officers and unit leaders—simple, stubborn men—rallied, chased down their commander, smashed his cage cart, and freed him from bonds.

sentences.zh: 艾在困地，是以狼狽失據。

translations.literal: Ai was in straitened ground; thereby he was wolf-coarse and lost footing.
translations.idiomatic: Caught in that desperate position, Deng Ai floundered without a foothold.

sentences.zh: 夫反非小事，若懷噁心，即當謀及豪傑，然後乃能興動大眾，不聞艾有腹心一人。

translations.literal: Now rebellion is no small matter; if harboring evil mind, then ought plot reaching heroes—afterward then able to rouse great masses; not heard that Ai had one belly-heart man.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion is no trifle; a true traitor first wins over bold leaders and only then can stir the masses—yet no one ever named a single confidant of Deng Ai.

sentences.zh: 臨死口無惡言，獨受腹背之誅，豈不哀哉！

translations.literal: Facing death mouth had no evil words; alone he received belly-back execution—is it not pitiable!
translations.idiomatic: He spoke no treason even facing death, yet was destroyed from front and back—is that not heartbreaking?

sentences.zh: 故見之者垂涕，聞之者歎息。

translations.literal: Therefore those who saw shed tears; those who heard sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Witnesses wept; everyone who heard the tale groaned.

sentences.zh: 此賈誼所以慷慨于漢文，天下之事可為痛哭者，良有以也。

translations.literal: This is why Jia Yi therefore was impassioned toward Han Wen—affairs under Heaven for which one may bitterly weep—truly there is cause.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Jia Yi poured out his grief to Emperor Wen of Han: some national wrongs truly merit bitter tears.

sentences.zh: 陛下龍興，闡弘大度，受誅之家，不拘敘用，聽艾立後，祭祀不絕。

translations.literal: Your Majesty dragon-rises; spreads vast magnanimity; houses that received execution are not barred from graded employment; allows Ai to establish an heir; sacrifices do not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty ascended the dragon throne you have shown magnificent generosity: families that suffered execution are not forever barred from office, and Deng Ai has been allowed an heir so his sacrifices continue.

sentences.zh: 昔秦人憐白起之無罪，吳人傷子胥之冤酷，皆為之立祠。

translations.literal: Formerly Qin people pitied Bai Qi's absence of crime; Wu people grieved Zixu's cruel injustice—both for them established shrines.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Qin mourned Bai Qi as innocent; the people of Wu ached over Wu Zixu's cruel fate—and shrines were raised to both.

sentences.zh: 天下之人為艾悼心痛恨，亦由是也。

translations.literal: Under Heaven's people for Ai mourn heart pain hatred—it is also from this.
translations.idiomatic: The empire's grief and outrage over Deng Ai spring from the same sentiment.

sentences.zh: 謂可聽艾門生故吏收艾屍柩，歸葬舊墓，還其田宅，以平蜀之功，繼封其後，使艾闔棺定諡，死無所恨。

translations.literal: I say it is permissible to allow Ai's disciples and former clerks to gather Ai's coffin; return burial to old tomb; restore his fields and houses; by merit of pacifying Shu, continue enfeoffment of his posterity; cause Ai coffin-closed fix posthumous title—dead without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Let his students and old subordinates recover his remains, bury him in the family plot, restore his lands and houses, ennoble his heirs for the Shu campaign, and settle his posthumous title once the lid is closed—then he can rest without resentment.

sentences.zh: 赦冤魂于黃泉，收信義於後世，則天下徇名之士，思立功之臣，必投湯火，樂為陛下死矣！

translations.literal: Pardon wronged souls in yellow springs; gather trust and righteousness in later ages—then under Heaven name-seeking gentlemen, ministers thinking to establish merit, surely will cast into boiling fire, gladly die for Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: Free an unjust ghost in the underworld and win good faith for generations to come, and every reputation-minded gentleman and ambitious commander will rush through fire for Your Majesty!

sentences.zh: 帝省表，甚嘉其意。

translations.literal: The emperor examined the memorial; greatly praised its intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and warmly approved its spirit.

sentences.zh: 灼後復陳時宜曰：

translations.literal: Zhuo afterward again presented timely suitability, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Later Duan Zhuo submitted further advice on policy of the moment:

sentences.zh: 臣聞天時不如地利，地利不如人和。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard: Heaven's timing is not as good as earth's advantage; earth's advantage is not as good as men's harmony.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that opportunity from Heaven counts less than terrain, and terrain counts less than unity among the people.

sentences.zh: 三里之城，五里之郭，圜圍而攻之，有不克者，此天時不如地利。

translations.literal: A wall three li, an outer wall five li—round-besiege and attack it; there are those not overcome—this is Heaven's timing not as good as earth's advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Take a tiny citadel ringed by attackers who still cannot crack it—that shows weather and luck lose to strong ground.

sentences.zh: 城非不高，池非不深，穀非不多，兵非不利，委而去之，此地利不如人和。

translations.literal: The walls not not high, the moats not not deep, grain not not much, weapons not not sharp—yet cast aside and leave them—this is earth's advantage not as good as men's harmony.
translations.idiomatic: High walls, deep moats, full granaries, and keen weapons still abandoned mean superior terrain cannot save a divided people.

sentences.zh: 然古之王者，非不先推恩德，結固人心。

translations.literal: Yet kings of antiquity were not ones who did not first extend grace and virtue, knotting firm men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet true kings of old always began by spreading kindness and binding hearts together.

sentences.zh: 人心苟和，雖三里之城，五里之郭，不可攻也。

translations.literal: Men's hearts if harmonious—though a wall three li, outer wall five li—not possible to attack.
translations.idiomatic: When hearts are united, even a pocket fortress cannot be stormed.

sentences.zh: 人心不和，雖金城湯池，不能守也。

translations.literal: Men's hearts if not harmonious—though metal walls, boiling moats—not able to guard.
translations.idiomatic: When hearts are divided, neither bronze ramparts nor boiling moats will hold.

sentences.zh: 臣推此以廣其義，舜彈五弦之琴，詠《南風》之詩，而天下自理，由堯人可比屋而封也。

translations.literal: Your servant pushes this to broaden its meaning: Shun plucked a five-string zither, intoned the poem South Wind, and under Heaven self-ordered—because Yao's people could house-by-house be enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: From this I broaden the point: Shun could rule the realm simply by playing his five-string lute and singing the South Wind ode, because Yao had left the people so virtuous that every household deserved a noble title.

sentences.zh: 曩者多難，奸雄屢起，攪亂眾心，刀鋸相乘，流死之孤，哀聲未絕。

translations.literal: Of late many hardships; treacherous heroes repeatedly arose; stirred and disturbed the multitude's hearts; knife and saw succeeded one another; drifting-death orphans—mourning sounds not yet ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Recent generations have suffered endless turmoil: warlords rose again and again, minds were poisoned, executions followed one after another, and the wailing of refugees has barely faded.

sentences.zh: 故臣以為陛下當深思遠念，杜漸防萌，彈琴詠詩，垂拱而已。

translations.literal: Therefore your servant thinks Your Majesty ought deeply think and far ponder; stop gradual, guard sprouts; pluck zither intone poems—hang robe sleeves only.
translations.idiomatic: So I urge Your Majesty to think deep and far, choke troubles at the bud, and govern chiefly by moral influence rather than constant interference.

sentences.zh: 其要莫若推恩以協和黎庶，故推恩足以保四海，不推恩不足以保妻子。

translations.literal: Its essential nothing like extending grace to harmonize black-haired commoners—therefore extending grace suffices to protect four seas; not extending grace does not suffice to protect wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing matters more than spreading kindness to unite the common people: generous rule secures the realm; stinginess cannot even protect one's own household.

sentences.zh: 是故唐堯以親睦九族為先，周文以刑于寡妻為急，明王聖主莫不先親後疏，自近及遠。

translations.literal: Therefore Tang Yao took intimate harmony of nine kindreds as first; Zhou Wen took model conduct toward few wife as urgent; enlightened kings sagely lords none did not first kin afterward distant, from near reaching far.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Yao of Tang began by harmonizing his nine clans, King Wen of Zhou by setting an example for his consort; no wise ruler ever neglected kin near at hand before reaching outward.

sentences.zh: 臣以為太宰、司徒、衛將軍三王宜留洛中鎮守，其餘諸王自州征足任者，年十五以上悉遣之國。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks Grand Tutor, Minister of Education, Guard General—three kings—ought remain in Luoyang center to guard; the rest of the kings whom provincial evaluation deems fit for duty, age fifteen and above all dispatch them to their states.
translations.idiomatic: I propose keeping the three princes who hold the posts of grand tutor, minister of education, and guard general in Luoyang to anchor the capital, while every other prince assessed at the provincial level as fit for duty and aged fifteen or older should be sent out to his fief.

sentences.zh: 為選中郎傅相，才兼文武，以輔佐之。

translations.literal: For them select central gentleman tutor-ministers, talent spanning civil and martial, to assist them.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint each a mentor and chief minister chosen from the palace corps, men competent in both civil and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 聽于其國繕修兵馬，廣布恩信。

translations.literal: Allow in their states repair troops and horses; broadly spread grace and trust.
translations.idiomatic: Let them drill troops and spread benevolent authority within their domains.

sentences.zh: 必撫下猶子，愛國如家，君臣分定，百世不遷，連城開地，為晉、魯、衛。

translations.literal: Surely they will soothe inferiors like sons; love state like home; lord-minister portions fixed; hundred generations not moved; linked cities open lands—become Jin, Lu, Wei.
translations.idiomatic: They will cherish subjects like children and the realm like their own household; lord and vassal roles stay fixed for generations; wide domains will stand like the old houses of Jin, Lu, and Wei.

sentences.zh: 所謂磐石之宗，天下服其強矣。

translations.literal: What is called clan of rock—under Heaven submits to its strength.
translations.idiomatic: That is the true rock-solid royal house, and the empire will respect its strength.

sentences.zh: 雖云割地，譬猶囊漏貯中，亦一家之有耳。

translations.literal: Though said to divide land, likened still to bag leaking stored within—it is also one family's possession only.
translations.idiomatic: Granting territory sounds like loss, yet it is wealth shifting inside one purse—it still stays within the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 若慮後世強大，自可豫為制度，使得推恩以分子弟。

translations.literal: If worried posterity strength great, naturally can beforehand make institutions, cause able to extend grace to divide sons and younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: If you fear future over-mighty princes, lay down rules now that allow estates to be subdivided among heirs.

sentences.zh: 如此則枝分葉布，稍自削小，漸使轉至萬國，亦後世之利，非所患也。

translations.literal: Thus then branches divide leaves spread; gradually self pare small; gradually cause turn arriving myriad states—also posterity's profit; not what is feared.
translations.idiomatic: Branches will spread and holdings shrink step by step until they resemble the myriad states of old—a benefit to later reigns, not a danger.

sentences.zh: 昔在漢世，諸呂自疑，內有硃虛、東牟之親，外有諸侯九國之強，故不敢動搖。

translations.literal: Formerly in Han age, various Lü self-doubt; inside had Zhu Xu, Dong Mou kin; outside had feudal lords nine states' strength—therefore dared not shake move.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han the Lü clan hesitated because inside court stood princes like Liu Zhang of Zhu Xu and Liu Xingju of Dong Mou, while outside nine powerful kingdoms watched—so they dared not strike.

sentences.zh: 於今之宜，諸侯強大，是為太山之固。

translations.literal: As for today's suitability, feudal lords strong great—this makes Mount Tai's firmness.
translations.idiomatic: For present needs, strong regional princes are the surest bulwark—solid as Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 非我族類，其心必異。

translations.literal: Not our clan kind—their hearts surely different.
translations.idiomatic: Those outside the royal kin will never share the same loyalty.

sentences.zh: 而魏法禁錮諸王，親戚隔絕，不祥莫大焉。

translations.literal: Yet Wei law imprisoned fetters various kings; kin and affines cut off—no ill omen greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wei law penned princes like criminals and severed family ties—nothing could be more ominous.

sentences.zh: 間者無故又瓜分天下，立五等諸侯。

translations.literal: Recently without cause again melon-divided under Heaven, establishing five-ranks feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the realm has again been carved into feudal allotments for no compelling reason, reviving the five-grade nobility.

sentences.zh: 上不象賢，下不議功，而是非雜糅，例受茅土。

translations.literal: Those above do not model themselves on the worthy; those below do not have merit weighed; yet right and wrong are tangled together, and by precedent all alike receive feudal soil.
translations.idiomatic: The throne mirrors no sage; the ranks earn no fair tally of deeds—yet rumor and truth are stirred into one pot, and everyone walks away clutching a slice of realm.

sentences.zh: 似權時之宜，非經久之制，將遂不改，此亦煩擾之人，漸亂之階也。

translations.literal: It resembles what suits a moment of expediency; it is not a lasting system; should it then be followed without change, this too is for troubled folk the gradual stairway of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: It answers the panic of the hour, not the architecture of generations; let it harden uncorrected and you hand troublemakers the bottom step toward ruin.

sentences.zh: 夫國之興也，由於九族親睦，黎庶協和；

translations.literal: Now in the rise of a state: it comes from the nine kindreds being intimate and harmonious, and the black-haired multitude being concordant.
translations.idiomatic: Realms climb when kin rings true and the common people breathe as one lung.

sentences.zh: 其衰也，在於骨肉疏絕，百姓離心。

translations.literal: In its decline: it lies in flesh and bone growing estranged and cut off, and the hundred surnames losing heart.
translations.idiomatic: They fall when blood thins to strangers and the crowd turns its face away.

sentences.zh: 故夏邦不安，伊尹歸殷；

translations.literal: Therefore when the Xia domain was not secure, Yi Yin returned to Yin.
translations.idiomatic: So when Xia shook apart, Yi Yin crossed home to Yin.

sentences.zh: 殷邦不和，呂氏入周。

translations.literal: When the Yin domain was not harmonious, the house of Lü entered Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin quarreled with itself, the Lü came west to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 殷監在於夏後，去事之誡，誠來事之鑒也。

translations.literal: Yin's mirror stands after Xia; the warning drawn from what has gone is truly the mirror for what will come.
translations.idiomatic: Shang learned staring at Xia's corpse; yesterday's lecture is tomorrow's lantern.

sentences.zh: 又陳曰：

translations.literal: Again he presented and said:
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on:

sentences.zh: 昔伐蜀，募取涼州兵馬、羌胡健兒，許以重報，五千餘人，隨艾討賊，功皆第一。

translations.literal: Formerly in attacking Shu they recruited Liangzhou troops and horses, Qiang and Hu stalwarts, promising heavy reward; more than five thousand followed Deng Ai to punish the rebels, and their merit was in every case of the first grade.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu fell, Liangzhou riders and lean Qiang and Hu fighters were sworn thick pay; five thousand marched with Deng Ai, and each brought home the highest tally on the scroll.

sentences.zh: 而《乙亥詔書》，州郡將督，不與中外軍同，雖在上功，無應封者。

translations.literal: Yet in the edict of the Yihai year, commandery and prefecture generals and supervisors were not treated the same as inner and outer armies; though they bore upper merit, there were none who matched criteria for enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: But the Yihai edict denied provincial captains parity with palace hosts and field armies—even deeds stamped "first class" won no patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 唯金城太守楊欣所領兵，以逼江由之勢，得封者三十人。

translations.literal: Only the troops led by Jincheng Administrator Yang Xin, by the circumstance of pressing Jiangyou, had thirty who obtained enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yang Xin's Jincheng column, pinning Jiangyou by the throat, saw thirty men raised to rank.

sentences.zh: 自金城以西，非在欣部，無一人封者。

translations.literal: From west of Jincheng, those not in Xin's division—not one was enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: West of Jincheng, outside Yang Xin's roster, not one soldier tasted title.

sentences.zh: 苟在中軍之例，雖下功必侯；

translations.literal: If they fell under central-army precedent, though merit was lower they would surely be marquises;
translations.idiomatic: Serve by central-army rule and modest stripes still bought a marquis's seal;

sentences.zh: 如在州郡，雖功高不封，非所謂近不重施，遠不遺恩之謂也。

translations.literal: if they were in commanderies and prefectures, though merit was high they were not enfeoffed—this is not what is called "near not doubling favors, far not leaving kindness aside."
translations.idiomatic: hold a provincial posting and towering deeds meant silence—hardly the old pledge that reward need not pile up near the throne while distant sweat is still remembered.

sentences.zh: 臣聞魚懸由於甘餌，勇夫死於重報。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that fish hang because of sweet bait, and brave men die on account of heavy reward.
translations.idiomatic: Sweet bait lifts fish from the stream; heavy coin buys the brave man's last breath.

sentences.zh: 故荊軻慕燕丹之義，專諸感闔閭之愛，匕首振于秦庭，吳刀耀於魚腹，視死如歸，豈不有由也哉！

translations.literal: Therefore Jing Ke admired the righteousness of Crown Prince Dan of Yan; Zhuan Zhu was stirred by Helü's kindness—the dagger gleamed in Qin's court, the Wu blade flashed from the fish's belly; they regarded death as returning home—was there not cause!
translations.idiomatic: So Jing Ke rode Yan Dan's honor and Zhuan Zhu answered Helü's favor—steel shocked the Qin hall, a blade leapt from the banquet fish—and both stepped toward death as toward their own hearth. Of course they did.

sentences.zh: 夫功名重賞，士之所競，不平致怨，由來久矣。

translations.literal: Now fame, merit, and heavy reward are what gentlemen contend for; injustice bringing resentment has been long standing.
translations.idiomatic: Glory and gold are what fighting spirits chase; grudges born of unfair scales are older than memory.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「屍鳩在桑，其子七兮。

translations.literal: The Classic of Poetry says: "The turtle dove on the mulberry—its chicks are seven.
translations.idiomatic: The Songs record: "On the mulberry sits the shijiu—seven chicks beneath her wing.

sentences.zh: 淑人君子，其儀一兮。

translations.literal: The good man, the gentleman—his bearing is one."
translations.idiomatic: The worthy man's measure never divides."

sentences.zh: 」臣以為此等宜蒙爵封。

translations.literal: " Your subject considers that men of this sort ought to receive noble rank and enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: " Men of that stamp deserve patents and fields—I would see them clothed in both.

sentences.zh: 灼前後陳事，輒見省覽。

translations.literal: Zhuo, presenting affairs before and after, was always granted review and reading.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo memorialized again and again—and each time the throne looked.

sentences.zh: 然身微宦孤，不見進序，乃取長假還鄉里。

translations.literal: Yet his person was lowly and his office solitary; he saw no advancement in sequence; therefore he took extended leave and returned to his village.
translations.idiomatic: Lowborn and alone in rank, he gained no step forward—so he claimed long leave and walked home.

sentences.zh: 臨去，遣息上表曰：

translations.literal: On the verge of going, he sent his son to submit a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Before he went, he had his son lay this plea before you:

sentences.zh: 臣受恩三世，剖符守境，試用無績，沈伏數年，犬馬之力，無所復堪。

translations.literal: Your subject has received grace through three reigns, split tallies and guarded borders; tried in office without achievement, sunk low several years; the strength of dog and horse has nothing further it can bear.
translations.idiomatic: Three reigns have clothed me in favor; I bore tally and march yet proved hollow; years vanished in the shadows—this old hound has no stride left.

sentences.zh: 陛下弘廣納之聽，采狂夫之言，原臣侵官之罪，不問幹忤之愆，天地恩厚，於臣足矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty broadly opens receptive hearing, adopts a madman's words, forgives your subject's crime of encroaching on office, does not inquire into the fault of blunt offense; Heaven and Earth are thick in kindness—for your subject it is enough.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty hears wide enough to heed a crank, forgave my overreach, and never punished blunt speech—such heaven-high mercy leaves me full.

sentences.zh: 臣聞忠臣之于其君，猶孝子之於其親：進則有欣然之慶，非貪官也；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the loyal minister toward his lord is like the filial son toward his parents: in advancing there is glad rejoicing—it is not greed for office;
translations.idiomatic: They say the faithful servant loves his lord as a dutiful son loves his parents: promotion sparks joy—not hunger for title;

sentences.zh: 退則有戚然之憂，非懷祿也。

translations.literal: in retiring there is sorrowful worry—it is not cherishing stipend.
translations.idiomatic: withdrawal brings ache—not clutching salary.

sentences.zh: 其意在於不忘光君榮親，情所不能已已者也。

translations.literal: The intention lies in not forgetting to brighten the lord and honor kin—it is what emotion cannot cease ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: The aim is only to lend luster to sovereign and kin—a longing that will not quiet.

sentences.zh: 臣伏自悼，私懷至恨：生長荒裔，而久在外任，自還抱疾，未嘗覲見，陛下竟不知臣何人，此臣之恨一也。

translations.literal: Your subject prostrates himself and mourns himself, privately harboring utmost regret: born and raised on a remote frontier, long assigned abroad; since returning bearing illness, never having had audience—Your Majesty still does not know who your subject is—this is regret one for your subject.
translations.idiomatic: I kneel in private grief nursing five wounds: raised beyond the rim, long posted far—since sickness drove me home I have never looked into your eyes; you barely know my name—that is my first regret.

sentences.zh: 遭運會之世，值有事之時，而不能垂功名於竹帛，此臣之恨二也。

translations.literal: Encountering an age of shifting fortune, meeting a time of affairs, yet unable to hang fame and merit on bamboo and silk—this is regret two for your subject.
translations.idiomatic: I drew breath in an age that shook yet left no brushstroke for me—that is my second regret.

sentences.zh: 逮事聖明之君，而尪悴羸劣，陳力又不能，當歸死於地下，此臣之恨三也。

translations.literal: Having reached service under a sage-bright lord, yet wizened, wasted, weak and inferior, unable to display strength—properly one should return and die underground—this is regret three for your subject.
translations.idiomatic: I finally serve a luminous sovereign too broken to lift my weight—I belong under the clay—that is my third regret.

sentences.zh: 哀二親早亡隕，兄弟並凋喪，孝敬無復施於家門，此臣之恨四也。

translations.literal: Grieving that both parents died young and fell; brothers together withered and perished; filial respect has nowhere further to be practiced at the gate—this is regret four for your subject.
translations.idiomatic: Parents fell early; brothers followed—I have no porch left for duty—that is my fourth regret.

sentences.zh: 夏之日忽以過，冬之夜尋復來，人生百歲，尚以為不足，而臣中年嬰災，此臣之恨五也。

translations.literal: Summer's days suddenly pass; winter's nights soon come again; human life a hundred years still deemed insufficient—yet your subject in middle years encountered calamity—this is regret five for your subject.
translations.idiomatic: Summer races off; winter nights circle back; even a century feels brief—yet disaster caught me midlife—that is my fifth regret.

sentences.zh: 慚日月之所養，愧昊蒼而無報，此臣之所以懷五恨而歎息，臨歸路而自悼者也。

translations.literal: Ashamed before what sun and moon nurture, shamed before vast azure without repayment—this is why your subject harbors five regrets and sighs, facing the road home and mourning himself.
translations.idiomatic: I blush before what sun and moon fed me and cannot repay the sky—so I nurse five sighs on the road toward home.

sentences.zh: 語有之曰：「華言虛也，至言實也，苦言藥也，甘言疾也。

translations.literal: A saying has it: "Ornate words are empty; utmost words are substance; bitter words are medicine; sweet words are sickness.
translations.idiomatic: The proverb runs: "Silken speech is hollow; plain truth weighs solid; bitter counsel cures; honeyed flattery sickens.

sentences.zh: 」臣欲言天下太平，而靈龜神狐未見，仙芝萐莆未生，麒麟未遊乎靈禽之囿，鳳皇未儀於太極之庭，此臣之所以不敢華言而為佞者也。

translations.literal: " Your subject wishes to speak that All Under Heaven is greatly pacified, yet spirit tortoise and divine fox have not appeared, immortal zhi and auspicious shapu have not sprouted, qilin has not roamed the garden of numinous birds, phoenix has not displayed deportment in the Grand Ultimate court—this is why your subject dare not speak ornate words and become a flatterer.
translations.idiomatic: " I long to cry "All is peace!"—yet no sacred tortoise or silver fox appears, no lucky fungi break soil, no qilin paces the royal aviary, no phoenix patterns the palace yard—so I refuse to varnish truth.

sentences.zh: 昔漢高祖初定天下，于時戍卒婁敬上書諫曰：「陛下取天下不與成周同，而欲比靈斯成周，臣竊以為不侔。

translations.literal: Formerly when Han Gaozu first settled All Under Heaven, at that time garrison soldier Lou Jing submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying: "Your Majesty's taking All Under Heaven is not the same as accomplished Zhou's; yet desiring to compare sacred fortune with accomplished Zhou, your subject privately thinks they do not match.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu first steadied the realm, the conscript Lou Jing warned: "You won the empire unlike the perfected Zhou—yet you mean to match their divine heyday; I cannot see the likeness.

sentences.zh: 」於是漢祖感悟，深納其言，賜姓為劉氏。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Han's ancestor was moved to insight, deeply accepted his words, and granted him the surname Liu.
translations.idiomatic: " The Han founder listened hard, took the lesson in full, and folded Lou Jing into the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 又顧謂陸賈曰：「為我著秦所以亡，而吾所以得之者。

translations.literal: Again he turned and said to Lu Jia: "For me write why Qin thus perished, and why I thus obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Lu Jia: "Set down how Qin fell and how I rose.

sentences.zh: 」賈乃作《新語》之書，述敘前世成敗，以為勸戒。

translations.literal: " Jia then composed the book New Discourses, narrating former generations' success and failure, as admonition and warning.
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Jia answered with his New Discourses, threading old victories and collapses into mirror and caution.

sentences.zh: 又田肯建一言之計，非親子弟莫可使王齊者，而受千金之賜。

translations.literal: Again Tian Ken proposed a plan of one sentence: none but intimate sons and younger brothers should be made kings of Qi—and received a gift of a thousand in gold.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Ken earned a fortune of gold with one sentence—only royal kin should rule Qi.

sentences.zh: 故世稱漢祖之寬明博納，所以能成帝業也。

translations.literal: Therefore the age praises Han Progenitor's breadth, clarity, and broad acceptance—thereby he was able to accomplish imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Hence men sing of Gaozu's wide mind—that was how he hammered out an empire.

sentences.zh: 今之言世者，皆曰堯舜復興，天下已太平矣。

translations.literal: Now those who speak of the age all say Yao and Shun have revived and All Under Heaven is already greatly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Today's chorus insists Yao and Shun walk again and the realm already sleeps in calm.

sentences.zh: 臣獨以為未，亦竊有所勸焉。

translations.literal: Your subject alone considers it not yet so, and also privately has something to urge.
translations.idiomatic: I alone say "not yet"—and beg leave to push one counsel.

sentences.zh: 且百王垂制，聖賢吐言，來事之明鑒也。

translations.literal: Moreover the hundred kings' suspended systems, sages and worthies' uttered words are bright mirrors for affairs to come.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the statutes kings left and phrases sages breathed out are lanterns for what follows.

sentences.zh: 孟子曰：「堯不能以天下與舜，則舜之有天下也，天與之也。

translations.literal: Mencius said: "If Yao could not give All Under Heaven to Shun, then Shun's possessing All Under Heaven was Heaven giving it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius wrote: "If Yao could not hand the realm to Shun, then Shun's throne was Heaven's gift.

sentences.zh: 昔舜為相，堯崩，三年之喪畢，舜避堯之子于南河，天下諸侯朝覲者、獄訟者，不之堯之子而之舜。

translations.literal: Formerly when Shun was minister, Yao died; when the three years' mourning ended, Shun yielded place to Yao's son at South River; of All Under Heaven's feudal lords who came to audience or brought lawsuits, none went to Yao's son but went to Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shun served as minister: Yao died; mourning ended; Shun withdrew south of the river before Yao's heir—yet every lord who sought judgment chose Shun's tent, not the boy's.

sentences.zh: 舜曰天也，乃之中國，踐天子位焉。

translations.literal: Shun said it was Heaven; then he went to the central domains and ascended the Son of Heaven's position.
translations.idiomatic: Shun called it Heaven's nod, entered the heartland, and mounted the throne.

sentences.zh: 若居堯之宮，逼堯之子，非天所與者也。

translations.literal: If one dwelt in Yao's palace and pressed Yao's son, that would not be what Heaven granted.
translations.idiomatic: Occupy Yao's halls and shoulder his heir aside—that is no heavenly mandate.

sentences.zh: 」曩昔西有不臣之蜀，東有僭號之吳，三主鼎足，並稱天子。

translations.literal: " Formerly to the west was Shu that did not submit as subject; to the east was Wu that usurped titles; three lords stood tripod-footed, together calling themselves Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " Once Shu in the west refused fealty; Wu in the east stole regalia—three kings balanced like tripod legs, each crying "Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 魏文帝率萬乘之眾，受禪於靡陂，而自以德同唐、虞，以為漢獻即是古之堯，自謂即是今之舜，乃謂孟柯、孫卿不通禪代之變，遂作禪代之文，刻石垂戒，班示天下，傳之後世，亦安能使將來君子皆曉然心服其義乎！

translations.literal: Wei Wendi led hosts of ten thousand chariots, received abdication at Mobei, and deemed his virtue matched Tang and Yu; he thought Emperor Xian was the Yao of antiquity and himself was the Shun of today—thereupon pronounced Meng Ke and Sun Qing ignorant of the changes of abdication succession; then composed texts on abdication succession, carved them in stone as hanging warning, promulgated display under Heaven, transmitted them to later ages—how could that ever make gentlemen yet to come all plainly understand in heart and submit to its righteousness!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei marched ten thousand chariots to Mobei for the abdication yet fancied himself Tang or Yu—Han Xiandi his ancient Yao, himself the modern Shun—then mocked Mencius and Xunzi for missing the ritual arithmetic of yielding thrones, etched sermons in stone, and mailed them to posterity—could that truly bend tomorrow's gentlemen to conviction?

sentences.zh: 然魏文徒希慕堯、舜之名，推新集之魏，欲以同于唐、虞之盛，忽骨肉之恩，忘籓屏之固，竟不能使四海賓服，混一皇化，而于時群臣莫有諫者，不其過矣哉！

translations.literal: Yet Wei Wen vainly yearned after Yao and Shun's names, promoted the newly gathered Wei, desired to align with Tang and Yu's splendor, neglected flesh-and-bone kindness, forgot screen-barrier solidity—ultimately could not make the four seas guest-submit and merge in imperial transformation—yet at that time among assembled ministers none remonstrated—is it not excessive fault!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wendi chased Yao-Shun glitter while hoisting young Wei, dreamed of Tang-Yu zeniths, shrugged off kin and frontier walls—never bent the four seas to one awe—and still no minister dared cough a warning: what failure was that?

sentences.zh: 孫卿曰：「堯、舜禪讓，是不然矣。

translations.literal: Sun Qing said: "Yao and Shun's yielding abdication—is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Xunzi objected: "That fairy tale about Yao yielding to Shun—no.

sentences.zh: 天下者，至重也，非至強莫之能任；

translations.literal: All Under Heaven is utmost heavy—not utmost strong and none can bear it;
translations.idiomatic: The realm weighs absolute—without supreme strength no shoulders lift it;

sentences.zh: 至大也，非至辯莫之能分；

translations.literal: utmost great—not utmost eloquent and none can divide it;
translations.idiomatic: it spans absolute breadth—without supreme discernment no mind maps it;

sentences.zh: 至眾也，非至明莫之能見。

translations.literal: utmost numerous—not utmost clear-sighted and none can see it.
translations.idiomatic: it teems beyond counting—without luminous judgment no eye masters it.

sentences.zh: 此三至者，非聖人莫之能盡。

translations.literal: These three ultimates—not a sage and none can exhaust them.
translations.idiomatic: Those three peaks only a sage can summit.

sentences.zh: 」由此言之，孫卿、孟軻亦各有所不取焉。

translations.literal: " From this speaking, Sun Qing and Meng Ke also each have what they do not accept.
translations.idiomatic: " Even Xunzi and Mencius carved chunks from each other's creed.

sentences.zh: 陛下受禪，從東府入西宮，兵刃耀天，旌旗翳日。

translations.literal: Your Majesty received abdication, went from Eastern Offices into Western Palace; weapons glittered to Heaven, banners shaded the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Your own succession ran from Eastern Annex to Western Palace—blade-light stabbed the sky, banners swallowed the sun.

sentences.zh: 雖應天順人，同符唐、虞，然法度損益，則亦不異于昔魏文矣，故宜資三至以強制之。

translations.literal: Although answering Heaven and obeying people, matching tally with Tang and Yu, yet in laws and measures decrease-increase then also not different from former Wei Wen—therefore it is fitting to rely on the three ultimates to strengthen and restrain it.
translations.idiomatic: You answered Heaven and men like Tang and Yu—yet the tweaks of statute echo Wei Wendi's handbook—so lean on those three ultimates and bolt the gate.

sentences.zh: 而今諸王有立國之名，而無襟帶之實。

translations.literal: Now the various kings have the name of establishing states, yet lack the substance of lapel-and-girdle terrain.
translations.idiomatic: Today princes wear kingdoms on paper yet hold no strategic belt of land.

sentences.zh: 又蜀地有自然之險，是曆世奸雄之所窺覦，逋逃之所聚也，而無親戚子弟之守，此豈深思遠慮，杜漸防萌者乎！

translations.literal: Moreover Shu territory has natural peril; it is what successive ages' crafty heroes covertly covet and where fugitives gather—yet there are no kin or sons and younger brothers guarding it—is this how one deeply thinks far plans, stops gradual onset and guards sprouts!
translations.idiomatic: Shu's cliffs tempt every schemer and shelter every outlaw—yet no royal cousins stand watch there: is that how wise men stamp sparks before they bloom?

sentences.zh: 昔漢文帝據已成之業，六合同風，天下一家。

translations.literal: Formerly Han Wendi occupied already accomplished enterprise; six directions shared one wind; All Under Heaven one family.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wendi inherited a finished realm—every quarter breathed one wind, the map one hearth.

sentences.zh: 而賈誼上疏陳當時之勢，猶以為譬如抱火厝於積薪之下，而寢其上，火未及然，因謂之安。

translations.literal: Yet Jia Yi submitted memorial stating the age's situation, still thinking it like embracing fire placed under piled kindling and sleeping atop it; fire had not yet burned—thereupon calling it secure.
translations.idiomatic: Still Jia Yi warned the throne was sleeping on stacked kindling with live coals tucked beneath—flames not yet licking—yet ministers called it safe.

sentences.zh: 此言誠存不忘亡，安不忘亂者也。

translations.literal: These words truly are preserving existence not forgetting perishing, in peace not forgetting chaos.
translations.idiomatic: That voice is the discipline of remembering ruin while you breathe and storm while you dine.

sentences.zh: 然臣之慺慺，亦竊願陛下居安思危，無曰高高在上，常念臨深之義，不忘履冰之戒。

translations.literal: Yet your subject's earnest sincerity also privately wishes Your Majesty in dwelling secure to think peril; do not say high-high above; constantly recall the meaning of overlooking the deep; not forget treading ice's warning.
translations.idiomatic: Yet my stubborn heart begs you: feast in peace but taste peril—never murmur that you float too high—keep the cliff's lip and thin ice underfoot.

sentences.zh: 盡除魏世之弊法，綏以新政之大化，使萬邦欣欣，喜戴洪惠，昆蟲草木，咸蒙恩澤。

translations.literal: Exhaustively remove Wei age's harmful laws; pacify with new government's great transformation; cause myriad regions joyful-joyful, gladly bearing vast kindness; insects and plants all receive grace-moisture.
translations.idiomatic: Scrub Wei's stale statutes, smooth the realm with fresh reform until every quarter laughs under broad favor—even weed and worm taste your rain.

sentences.zh: 朝廷詠康哉之歌，山藪無伐檀之人，此固天下所視望者也。

translations.literal: Court recites the Kang-zai song; mountains and marshes have none who fell sandalwood—this indeed is what All Under Heaven looks toward.
translations.idiomatic: Let ministers hymn the "how peaceful" verse and leave hills free of sandalwood thieves—that is what the world cranes to see.

sentences.zh: 陛下自初踐阼，發無諱之詔，置箴諫之官，赫然寵異諤諤之臣，以明好直言之信，恐陳事者知直言之不用，皆杜口結舌，祥瑞亦曷由來哉！

translations.literal: Your Majesty from your first treading of the throne issued edicts without taboo, established remonstrance officials, brilliantly favored and distinguished outspoken ministers, to clarify faith in loving blunt speech—lest those who present affairs know blunt speech is not used, all seal mouths and tie tongues—how then would auspicious omens come!
translations.idiomatic: From your first step on the throne you pledged blunt counsel, installed critic posts, and lifted noisy dissenters high—yet if speakers learn honesty buys silence, lips weld shut and omens lose their road to court.

sentences.zh: 臣無陸生之才，不在顧問之地，蓋聞主聖臣直，義在於有犯無隱。

translations.literal: Your subject lacks Master Lu's talent and is not in counsel's place; your subject has heard that when the lord is sage the ministers are straight—the righteousness lies in risking offense without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: I am no Lu Jia; I do not sit in your advisory circle—yet they say a holy lord welcomes blunt servants: duty is to risk offense and hide nothing.

sentences.zh: 臣不惟疏遠，未信而言，敢曆論前代隆名之君及亡敗之主廢興所由，又博陳舉賢之路，廣開養老之制，崇必信之道，又張設議者之難，凡五事以聞。

translations.literal: Your subject not only is distant and estranged, untrusted yet speaking—dares serially discuss former generations' sovereigns of lofty fame and ruined defeated lords' rise-fall causes; again broadly presents paths for raising worthies, broadly opens systems for nurturing old age, exalts ways of certain faith; again spreads out debaters' difficulties—in all five matters to report.
translations.idiomatic: Remote and never proven, I still presume to trace how famed kings rose and fallen tyrants sank; I widen roads for talent, broaden care for elders, lift honest dealing, and lay out what critics will fight—in five threads for your ear.

sentences.zh: 臣之所言，皆直陳古今已行故事，非新聲異端也。

translations.literal: What your subject speaks all bluntly states antiquity and today's already practiced precedents; it is not new tunes or heterodox doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Every line I offer walks worn grooves of old and recent precedent—no novelty, no heresy.

sentences.zh: 辭義實淺，不足採納。

translations.literal: The wording's meaning is truly shallow, insufficient to be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The phrasing stays shallow—hardly worth lifting wholesale.

sentences.zh: 然臣私心，誠謂有可發起覺悟遺忘。

translations.literal: Yet your subject's private heart truly says there is what can stir awakening of forgotten things.
translations.idiomatic: Still I believe it may jog memory on points half sleeping.

sentences.zh: 願陛下察臣愚忠，湣臣狂直，無使天下以言者為戒。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty observe your subject's foolish loyalty, pity your subject's mad bluntness; do not cause All Under Heaven to take speakers as warning.
translations.idiomatic: See my clumsy loyalty, pity my rash tongue—do not teach the realm that speech is peril.

sentences.zh: 疾痛增篤，退念桑梓之詩，惟狐死之義，輒取長休，歸近墳墓。

translations.literal: Your subject's illness and pain grew severe; recalling the mulberry-and-catalpa poem and the lesson that the fox faces its burial mound, your subject then took long rest, returning near tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Pain gnaws deeper; I remember the ode of home and the fox who faces its mound—I claim long leave and crawl toward family graves.

sentences.zh: 顧瞻宮闕，系情皇極，不勝丹款，遣息穎表言。

translations.literal: Looking toward palace gate-towers, tying feeling to the august pole, unable to bear crimson sincerity—your subject sends his son Ying to memorialize speech.
translations.idiomatic: Though my eyes cling to your towers and my heart locks on the throne, this honest ache overflows—so I send my son Ying to carry these words.

sentences.zh: 其一曰：臣聞善有章也，著在經典；

translations.literal: The first says: your subject has heard good has manifest regulation—it is written in classics;
translations.idiomatic: First: I am told virtue wears bright badges—the canon says so;

sentences.zh: 惡有罰也，戒在刑書。

translations.literal: evil has punishment—it is warned in penal writings.
translations.idiomatic: evil carries stripes—the statute scroll says so.

sentences.zh: 上自遠古，下洎秦、漢，其明王霸主及亡國暗君，故可得而稱；

translations.literal: Above from remote antiquity, below down to Qin and Han—their enlightened kings, hegemonic lords, and ruined-state dark sovereigns—thus can be named and cited;
translations.idiomatic: From deepest antiquity down through Qin and Han, shining kings, league champions, and extinguished fools can still be named;

sentences.zh: 至於忠蹇賢相及佞諂奸臣，亦可得而言。

translations.literal: As for loyal obstructive worthy chancellors and flattery-murmuring treacherous ministers—also can be spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: so can blunt loyal ministers and smiling traitors.

sentences.zh: 故朝有諤諤盡規之臣，無不昌也；

translations.literal: Therefore courts having outspoken exhaust-remonstrance ministers—none do not flourish;
translations.idiomatic: Courts noisy with critics thrive;

sentences.zh: 任用阿諛唯唯之士，無不亡也。

translations.literal: employing fawning yes-yes gentlemen—none do not perish.
translations.idiomatic: courts stuffed with nodding flatterers rot.

sentences.zh: 是有國者皆欲求忠以自輔，舉賢以自佐；

translations.literal: Therefore those who possess states all desire seeking loyalty to assist themselves, raising worthies to aid themselves;
translations.idiomatic: Every holder of a realm claims to want loyal hands and worthy aides;

sentences.zh: 而亡國破家者相繼，皆由任失其人。

translations.literal: yet ruined-state broken-house ones succeed one another—all come from appointment losing the right men.
translations.idiomatic: yet dynasties fall in rows because the wrong faces fill the chairs.

sentences.zh: 所謂賢者不賢，忠者不忠也。

translations.literal: What is called worthy is not worthy; what is called loyal is not loyal.
translations.idiomatic: They praise worth yet seat mediocrity; cry loyalty yet harbor wolves.

sentences.zh: 臣謹言前任賢所由興，任不肖所以亡者。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully speaks of former employing worthies' whereby rise, employing unworthies' whereby perishing.
translations.idiomatic: Let me trace how wise appointments built thrones and foolish ones pulled them down.

sentences.zh: 堯之末年，四凶在朝而不去，八元在家而不舉，然致天平地寧，四門穆穆，其功固在重華之為相。

translations.literal: In Yao's late years, four villains were at court yet not removed; eight yuan were at home yet not raised—yet he brought Heaven flat and earth tranquil, four gates august-quiet—the achievement indeed lay in Chonghua's serving as minister.
translations.idiomatic: Late Yao kept four monsters in hall and eight talents in obscurity—yet heaven steadied and gates grew solemn because Shun as minister steadied the helm.

sentences.zh: 夏癸放於鳴條，商辛梟於牧野，此俱萬乘之主，而國滅身擒，由不能屬任賢相，用婦人之言，荒淫無道，肆志沈宴，作靡靡之樂，長夜之飲，於是登糟丘，臨酒池，觀牛飲，望肉林，龍逢忠而被害，比干諫而剖心，天下之所以歸惡者也。

translations.literal: Xia Gui was banished at Mingtiao; Shang Xin was executed-and-displayed at Muye—these both were lords of ten thousand chariots, yet state extinguished and person captured—because they could not entrust succession to worthy chancellors, employed women's words, were dissolute without way, indulged will in sinking banquets, made dissolving-dissolving music, long-night drinking; thereupon ascended lees-mound, overlooked wine pool, watched ox-drinking, gazed on meat forest; Longfeng was loyal yet harmed, Bi Gan remonstrated yet heart cut out—this is why All Under Heaven turned evil toward them.
translations.idiomatic: Jie fell at Mingtiao; Zhou's head answered Muye—both rode ten thousand chariots yet lost realm and liberty because they spurned wise ministers, obeyed women's whispers, drowned in lust and night-long cups, built hills of dregs and seas of wine, staged herd drinking under forests of meat—Longfeng died loyal, Bi Gan's heart was carved out for speaking—and the world learned to hate them.

sentences.zh: 太甲暴虐，顛覆湯之典制，於是伊尹放之桐宮，而能改悔反善，三年而後歸於亳。

translations.literal: Taijia was cruel and tyrannical, overturned Tang's statutes and systems; thereupon Yi Yin banished him to Tong Palace, and he was able to reform regret and return to good; after three years then returned to Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Taijia shattered Tang's laws until Yi Yin locked him in Tong Palace—where shame turned him decent and three years later he reclaimed Bo.

sentences.zh: 既已放而復還，殷道微而復興，諸侯咸服，號稱太宗，實賴阿衡之盡忠也。

translations.literal: Already having been banished yet returning, Yin way faint yet reviving, feudal lords all submitted, titled Grand Ancestor—it truly depended on Ah Heng's exhausting loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Banished yet welcomed back, Yin rallied thin blood until lords bowed and histories crowned him Grand Ancestor—all credit to Yi Yin the Regent's stubborn faith.

sentences.zh: 周室既衰，諸侯並爭，天王微弱，政遂陵遲。

translations.literal: Zhou house already declined, feudal lords together contended; Heavenly King was weak slight; governance then slid downhill.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou faded while barons clawed each other—the Son of Heaven shrank and government slid downhill.

sentences.zh: 齊桓公，淫亂之主耳；

translations.literal: Duke Huan of Qi—merely a dissolute-disorderly lord;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi was a rake at heart;

sentences.zh: 然所以能九合一匡之功，有尊周之名，誠管夷吾之力。

translations.literal: Yet the reason he could achieve nine assemblies one rectification's merit, possess honoring Zhou's fame—truly was Guan Yiwu's strength.
translations.idiomatic: yet nine leagues and one rescue of order, plus fame as Zhou's shield, rode wholly on Guan Zhong's spine.

sentences.zh: 及其死也，蟲流出門，豈非任豎貂之過乎！

translations.literal: When it came to his death, worms flowed out the gate—is it not fault of employing Shu Diao!
translations.idiomatic: When he died maggots crawled from his hall—price of trusting Shu Diao!

sentences.zh: 且一桓公之身，得管仲，其功如彼；

translations.literal: Moreover one Duke Huan's person—obtaining Guan Zhong—his merit was like that;
translations.idiomatic: One man named Huan with Guan Zhong wrought miracles;

sentences.zh: 用豎貂，其亂如此。

translations.literal: employing Shu Diao—his disorder was like this.
translations.idiomatic: trust Shu Diao and rot sets in overnight.

sentences.zh: 夫榮辱存亡，實在所任，可不審哉！

translations.literal: Now glory-disgrace survival-perishing truly lie in whom one appoints—can one not examine!
translations.idiomatic: Glory or ruin rides on your roster—choose with both eyes open!

sentences.zh: 秦本伯翳之後，微微小邑，至秦仲始大，有車馬禮樂侍御之好焉。

translations.literal: Qin originally was descendant of Boyi—a tiny petty town; reaching Duke Zhong of Qin it began great, having chariot-horse rites-music attendant-driver fondness therein.
translations.idiomatic: Qin sprang from Boyi's blood as a flyspeck fort until Duke Zhong swelled it enough to fancy chariots, drums, and polished harness.

sentences.zh: 自穆公至於始皇，皆能留心待賢，遠求異士，招由余於西戎，致五羖于宛市，取丕豹于晉鄉，迎蹇叔于宗裏。

translations.literal: From Duke Mu down to First Emperor, all were able to fix heart on awaiting worthies, seek afar for unusual gentlemen—summoned You Yu from western Rong, brought five black rams at Wan market, took Pi Bao from Jin countryside, welcomed Jian Shu from Zong hamlet.
translations.idiomatic: From Duke Mu to the First Emperor every lord hunted strangers with patience—You Yu from the western tribes, Baili Xi bought with five skins in Wan, Pi Bao stolen from Jin soil, Jian Shu coaxed from Zong lane.

sentences.zh: 由是四方雄俊繼踵而至，故能世為強國，吞滅諸侯，奄有天下，兼稱皇帝，由謀臣之助也。

translations.literal: From this the stalwart men of the four quarters followed heel-to-heel and came; therefore able generation after generation to be a strong state, swallow and extinguish the feudal lords, cover and possess all under Heaven, together be called emperor—it was by planning ministers' aid.
translations.idiomatic: Men of ability arrived from every quarter in succession, which allowed Qin for generations to remain a great power, annex the regional lords, rule the realm, and claim the imperial title: the strategists made it possible.

sentences.zh: 道化未淳，崩於沙丘。

translations.literal: The transforming influence was not yet pure; he collapsed at Shaqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Moral sway had not fully taken hold when he died at Shaqiu.

sentences.zh: 胡亥乘虐，用詐自悮，不能弘濟統緒，克成堂構，而乃殘賊仁義，毒流黔首。

translations.literal: Hu Hai rode cruelty, used deceit and misled himself, could not broadly rescue the dynastic succession thread and complete the hall-and-frame task; instead he mutilated benevolence and rightness, and poison spread to the black-haired commoners.
translations.idiomatic: The Second Emperor exploited cruelty and deceit, failed to preserve the line or finish his father's work, attacked morality itself, and brought ruin upon the people.

sentences.zh: 故陳勝、吳廣，奮臂大呼，而天下回應。

translations.literal: Therefore Chen Sheng and Wu Guang raised arms and shouted loudly, and all under Heaven responded.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Sheng and Wu Guang rose with a cry that drew response across the empire.

sentences.zh: 於是趙高逆亂，閻樂承指，二世窮迫，自戮望夷。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhao Gao rebelled in disorder; Yan Le carried out his intent; the Second Emperor, driven to extremity, killed himself at Wangyi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gao turned traitor, Yan Le executed his orders, and the trapped Second Emperor committed suicide at Wangyi.

sentences.zh: 子嬰雖立，去帝為王，孤危無輔，四旬而亡。

translations.literal: Although Ziying was enthroned, he removed the emperor title and became king; orphaned and imperiled without support, in forty days he perished.
translations.idiomatic: Ziying ruled only as king, not emperor; isolated and without allies, he fell within forty days.

sentences.zh: 此由邪臣擅命，指鹿為馬，所以速秦之禍也。

translations.literal: This was because wicked ministers monopolized commands, pointed at a deer and called it a horse—therefore Qin's calamity came swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked ministers seized authority and inverted truth—calling a deer a horse—which hastened Qin's ruin.

sentences.zh: 秦失其鹿，豪傑競逐，項羽既得而失之，其咎在烹韓生，而范增之謀不用。

translations.literal: When Qin forfeited the realm, stalwart men raced to seize it; Xiang Yu gained it yet lost it; the blame lies in boiling Han Sheng alive and not employing Fan Zeng's plans.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin lost control, contenders strove for mastery; Xiang Yu gained the upper hand then squandered it by executing Han Sheng and rejecting Fan Zeng's counsel.

sentences.zh: 假令羽既距項伯之邪說，斬沛公於鴻門，都咸陽以號令諸侯，則天下無敵矣。

translations.literal: Suppose Yu had rejected Xiang Bo's perverse counsel, executed the Lord of Pei at Hongmen, and made Xianyang his capital to command the feudal lords—then none under Heaven could have matched him.
translations.idiomatic: Had he dismissed Xiang Bo's bad advice, killed Liu Bang at Hongmen, and ruled from Xianyang over the lords, he would have been unbeatable.

sentences.zh: 而羽距韓生之忠諫，背范增之深計，自謂霸王之業已定，都彭城，還故鄉，為晝被文繡，此蓋世俗兒女之情耳，而羽榮之。

translations.literal: Yet Yu rejected Han Sheng's loyal remonstrance, turned his back on Fan Zeng's deep plans, deemed the work of the Hegemon-King already settled, made Pengcheng his capital, returned to his homeland, and dressed by day in patterned embroidery—this was merely the sentiment of vulgar sons and daughters, yet Yu gloried in it.
translations.idiomatic: He spurned Han Sheng's frank advice and Fan Zeng's strategy, assumed the hegemon's task finished, fixed his capital at Pengcheng, went home in triumph, and flaunted silk by day—petty vanity he mistook for glory.

sentences.zh: 是故五載為漢所擒，至此尚不知覺悟，乃曰「天亡我，非戰之罪」，甚痛矣哉！

translations.literal: Therefore in five years he was captured by Han; even then he still did not awaken, and said, "Heaven destroys me, not the fault of war"—how bitter indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Within five years Han took him prisoner; still unrepentant, he blamed Heaven rather than his generalship—a grievous blindness.

sentences.zh: 且夫士之歸仁，猶水之歸下，禽之走曠野，故曰「為川驅魚者獺也，為藪驅雀者鸇也，為湯、武驅人者桀、紂也。

translations.literal: Moreover, scholars turning to benevolence is like water flowing downward and birds fleeing to the open wilds; hence it is said, "For the river that drives the fish is the otter; for the marsh that drives the sparrows is the hawk; for Tang and Wu that drive the people are Jie and Zhou."
translations.idiomatic: Men drawn to humane rule behave like water seeking low ground; hence the saying that tyrants drive the people to founders worthy as Tang and Wu—as predators scatter smaller creatures.

sentences.zh: 」漢高祖起于布衣，提三尺之刃而取天下，用六國之資，無唐、虞之禪，豈徒賴良、平之奇謀，盡英雄之智力而已乎，亦由項 氏為驅人也。

translations.literal: The Han founder rose from common cloth, grasped a three-foot blade and took all under Heaven, used the resources of the six states, without Tang and Yu-style abdication—was it only by relying on Liang and Ping's singular stratagems and exhausting heroes' wit and strength? It was also because the Xiang clan drove the people for him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bang rose from common ranks with a sword, conquered the realm with the former states' wealth, and seized power without the gracious abdications of antiquity. His success rested not only on Zhang Liang and Chen Ping but also on how the Xiang clan alienated the populace.

sentences.zh: 子孫承基二百餘年，逮成帝委政舅家，使權勢外移。

translations.literal: Sons and grandsons inherited the foundation for over two hundred years; until Chengdi entrusted government to his mother's clan and shifted power and influence outward.
translations.idiomatic: Han heirs held the throne for more than two centuries until Emperor Cheng handed authority to his maternal kin and influence drained from the court.

sentences.zh: 安昌侯張禹者，漢之三公，成帝保傅也，帝親幸其家，拜禹床下，深問天災人事。

translations.literal: Lord Anchang Zhang Yu was one of Han's Three Dukes and Chengdi's tutor; the emperor personally favored his house, bowed beneath Zhang Yu's couch, and deeply asked about heavenly calamities and human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu of Anchang ranked among the Three Dukes and tutored Emperor Cheng; the sovereign visited him at home, bowed before his seat, and questioned him closely about omens and policy.

sentences.zh: 禹當惟大臣之節，為社稷深慮，忠言嘉謀，陳其災患，則王氏不得專權寵，王莽無緣乘勢位，遂托雲龍而登天衢，令漢祚中絕也。

translations.literal: Yu ought to have upheld a great minister's integrity, pondered deeply for the altars of soil and grain, offered loyal words and fine plans, and set forth the disasters—then the Wang clan could not have monopolized favor and power, Wang Mang would have had no opening to ride circumstance and position, pretend to cloud-dragon omens, ascend the high road, and cut off Han's mandate midway.
translations.idiomatic: Had Zhang Yu acted as a chief minister should—counseling frankly on dangers to the dynasty—the Wangs might not have monopolized power, nor Wang Mang climbed the throne on forged portents and ended Han's line.

sentences.zh: 禹佞諂不忠，挾懷私計，徒低仰于五侯之間，苟取容媚而已。

translations.literal: Yu was flattering and unfaithful, harbored private calculations, merely bobbed up and down among the Five Marquises, and sought only to ingratiate himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu flattered and schemed, shuttling among the Five Marquises to save his own skin.

sentences.zh: 是以硃雲抗節求尚方斬馬劍，欲以斬禹，以戒其餘，可謂忠矣。

translations.literal: Therefore Zhu Yun held fast to integrity and sought the palace sword to behead a horse, wishing to execute Yu and warn the rest—this may be called loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yun demanded the imperial executioner's blade to strike Zhang Yu down and warn others—a courageous loyalty.

sentences.zh: 而成帝尚復不寤，乃以為居下訕上，廷辱保傅，罪死無赦，詔御史將雲下，欲急烹之。

translations.literal: Yet Chengdi still did not wake; he deemed it slandering superiors from below and publicly humiliating his tutor, a crime deserving death without pardon; he ordered the imperial clerk to take Yun down and wished to boil him quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdi remained obtuse, treating the protest as insult to his tutor and a capital offense; he ordered guards to seize Zhu Yun and would have executed him summarily.

sentences.zh: 雲攀殿折檻，幸賴左將軍辛慶忌叩頭流血，以死爭之。

translations.literal: Yun climbed the hall and broke the railing; fortunately he relied on General of the Left Xin Qingji knocking his head until it bled, disputing with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yun clung to the palace balustrade until it broke; Xin Qingji saved him by battering his brow in desperate appeal.

sentences.zh: 若不然，則雲已摧碎矣。

translations.literal: Had it not been so, then Yun would already have been shattered.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise Zhu Yun would have been destroyed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 後雖釋檻不修，欲以彰明直臣，誠足以為後世之戒，何益於漢室所由亡也哉！

translations.literal: Though later they released him and did not repair the railing, wishing thereby to display upright ministers, truly it could serve as a warning to later ages—what good did it do for the reason Han thereby perished!
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the railing unrepaired honored blunt counsel for posterity, yet it did nothing to halt the dynasty's decline.

sentences.zh: 然世之論者以為亂臣賊子無道之甚者莫過於莽，此亦猶紂之不善不如是之甚也。

translations.literal: Yet worldly debaters hold that among rebellious ministers and wicked sons none surpasses Mang in utter lack of the Way—this also resembles claiming King Zhou's evil did not reach such an extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators call Wang Mang history's worst traitor—yet that verdict exaggerates evil much as lore exaggerates King Zhou.

sentences.zh: 傳稱莽始起外戚，折節力行，以要名譽，宗族稱孝，朋友歸仁。

translations.literal: The traditions say Mang first rose as an outer-court kinsman, curbed himself and practiced earnest conduct to win reputation; his lineage praised his filial piety, friends trusted his benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Accounts describe Wang Mang beginning as a maternal relative who tempered himself for reputation: kin praised his filial piety, friends his humane conduct.

sentences.zh: 及其輔政成、哀之際，勤勞國家，動見稱述。
