translations.literal: When he assisted government under Cheng and Ai, he toiled for the state and his deeds won praise.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister under Emperors Cheng and Ai, he labored for the state and earned widespread commendation.

sentences.zh: 然于時人士詣闕上書薦莽者不可稱紀，內外群臣莫不歸莽功德。

translations.literal: At that time gentlemen who went to the palace gate to submit memorials recommending Mang were beyond counting; within and without, no minister failed to ascribe merit and virtue to Mang.
translations.idiomatic: Men petitioned endlessly at the palace gates to praise him; officials everywhere credited him with merit and virtue.

sentences.zh: 遭遇漢室中微，國嗣三絕，而太后壽考，為之宗主，故莽得遂策命孺子而奪其位也。

translations.literal: Meeting Han's mid-dynasty decline, the imperial heir cut off thrice, while the Grand Empress Dowager lived long as clan head—thus Mang could carry out the investiture of the child emperor and seize his throne.
translations.idiomatic: Han weakened mid-reign, the succession failed three times, and the aged Grand Empress Dowager headed the clan—so Mang invested the child emperor and took the throne.

sentences.zh: 昔湯、武之興，亦逆取而順守之耳。

translations.literal: Formerly Tang and Wu's rise also seized first and guarded afterward with righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Tang and Wu had likewise seized power first, then ruled legitimately.

sentences.zh: 向莽深惟殷、周取守之術，崇道德，務仁義，履信實，去華偽，施惠天下，十有八年，恩足以感百姓，義足以結英雄，人懷其德，豪傑並用，如此，宗廟社稷宜未滅也，光武雖復賢才，大業詎可冀哉！

translations.literal: Had Mang reflected deeply on Yin and Zhou's methods of taking and holding power, honored virtue, pursued benevolence and rightness, practiced good faith, cast off show and deceit, spread kindness across the realm for eighteen years until his kindness moved the common people and his righteousness bound the heroes, each cherishing his virtue and stalwarts serving together—then the ancestral temples and altars might not yet have fallen; even if Guangwu were gifted, how could great enterprise be hoped for!
translations.idiomatic: Had Wang Mang studied how Shang and Zhou took and kept power—ruling with virtue, faith, and generosity for eighteen years until people and heroes rallied—Han shrines might still stand; even a talented Guangwu could hardly have founded his cause.

sentences.zh: 莽即位之後，自謂得天人之助，以為功廣三王，德茂唐、虞，乃自驕矜，奮其威詐，班宣符讖，震暴殘酷，窮凶極惡，人怨神怒，冬雷電以驚其耳目，夏地動以惕其心腹。

translations.literal: After Mang took the throne he deemed himself aided by Heaven and man, thought his merit surpassed the Three Kings and his virtue outshone Tang and Yu; then he grew arrogant, wielded terror and deceit, promulgated talisman prophecies, shook the realm with cruelty, exhausted villainy and evil; men resented and spirits raged—winter thunder struck his ears and eyes, summer earthquakes warned his heart and belly.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned, Wang Mang claimed Heaven's blessing, fancied himself greater than the sage-kings, grew arrogant, ruled by terror and forged omens, and outdid cruelty until omens alarmed him—winter thunder, summer quakes.

sentences.zh: 而莽猶不知覺悟，方復重行不順時之令，竟連伍之刑，佞媚者親幸，忠諫者誅夷。

translations.literal: Yet Mang still did not awaken; he again enforced untimely ordinances, linked-neighborhood punishments, favored flatterers, and slaughtered loyal remonstrators.
translations.idiomatic: He still did not reform: harsh laws, collective punishment, favor for sycophants, and execution of honest critics.

sentences.zh: 由是天下忿憤，內外俱發，四海分崩，城池不守，身死於匹夫之手，為天下笑，豈不異哉！

translations.literal: Therefore all under Heaven burned with anger; inside and outside rose together; the four seas split apart; cities could not be held; he died at the hands of a common man and became the laughingstock of the realm—is this not strange!
translations.idiomatic: The empire erupted in rage, realms fragmented, defenses collapsed, and he fell to a common assassin—a spectacle of folly.

sentences.zh: 其所由然者，非取之過，而守之非道也。

translations.literal: The reason lies not in taking power wrongly but in guarding it without the Way.
translations.idiomatic: The fault was not seizing power but ruling without moral methods.

sentences.zh: 莽既屠肌，六合雲擾，劉聖公已立而不辨，盆子承之而覆敗，公孫述又稱帝於蜀漢。

translations.literal: Once Mang had devastated flesh and bone, the six directions churned like clouds; Liu Shengong was enthroned yet could not tell friend from foe; Penzi succeeded him and overturned in defeat; Gongsun Shu again declared himself emperor in Shu-Han.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Mang's ruin the realm convulsed: Liu Xuan ruled without clarity, Fan Penzi followed and failed, and Gongsun Shu claimed the throne in Shu.

sentences.zh: 如此數子，固非所謂應天順人者，徒為光武之驅除者耳。

translations.literal: Such men were indeed not those called responsive to Heaven and obedient to men; they merely cleared the path for Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: They were no true heirs of Heaven's mandate; they only swept the road for Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 夫天下者，蓋亦天下之天下，非一人之天下也。

translations.literal: All under Heaven is, in the end, the realm's realm, not one man's realm.
translations.idiomatic: The empire belongs to the world, not to a single ruler.

sentences.zh: 「殷商之旅，其會如林，矢於牧野，維予侯興。

translations.literal: "The hosts of Yin-Shang, their gathering like a forest; they arrayed themselves at Muye—in us the marches rise."
translations.idiomatic: "Shang's army gathered thick as a forest at Muye and pledged: it is we, the border lords, who rise."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「侯服于周，天命靡常。

translations.literal: "It is further said: The noble domains submit to Zhou; Heaven's mandate is not constant."
translations.idiomatic: "And: the royal domains bow to Zhou, for Heaven's mandate shifts."

sentences.zh: 」由此言之，主非常人也，有德則天下歸之，無德則天下叛之。

translations.literal: From this speaking, the ruler is no ordinary man: with virtue all under Heaven submits; without virtue all under Heaven rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the sovereign is no common person: virtue draws allegiance; its absence breeds revolt.

sentences.zh: 故古之明王，其勞心遠慮，常如臨川無津涯。

translations.literal: Therefore the enlightened kings of antiquity toiled their hearts and planned far, constantly as if facing a river without ford or shore.
translations.idiomatic: Wise kings of old worried and planned ahead as though standing before a river without crossing.

sentences.zh: 於是法天地，象四時，隆恩德，敬大臣，近忠直，遠佞人。

translations.literal: Thereupon they modeled Heaven and Earth, mirrored the four seasons, enlarged kindness and virtue, revered great ministers, drew near the loyal and upright, kept distance from flatterers.
translations.idiomatic: They took Heaven and Earth as models, matched the seasons, cultivated kindness, honored senior ministers, favored the loyal, and shunned flatterers.

sentences.zh: 仁孝著乎宮牆，弘化洽乎兆庶；

translations.literal: Benevolence and filial piety showed within the palace walls; broad transforming influence harmonized the myriad commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Filial devotion showed inside the palace; humane rule reached the common people.

sentences.zh: 為平直如砥矢，信義感人神。

translations.literal: Their conduct was straight and level as whetstone and arrow-shafts; good faith and rightness moved men and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Their ways were straight as a level line; sincerity moved both men and spirits.

sentences.zh: 雖有椒房外戚之寵，不受其委曲之言；

translations.literal: Though there were favorites from the inner chambers and maternal kin, they did not accept their twisting words.
translations.idiomatic: Despite palace favorites and in-laws, they refused twisted pleas.

sentences.zh: 雖有近習愛幸之豎，不聽其姑息之辭。

translations.literal: Though there were trusted attendants and darling eunuchs, they did not heed their indulgent pleas.
translations.idiomatic: Despite intimate servants and favored eunuchs, they ignored indulgent words.

sentences.zh: 四門穆穆，辟而不闔，待諫者而無忌。

translations.literal: The four gates stood solemn, open and unshut, awaiting remonstrators without taboo.
translations.idiomatic: The four gates stood open and solemn, welcoming critics without restriction.

sentences.zh: 恆戰戰慄栗，不忘戒懼，所以欲永終天祿，恐為將來賢 聖之驅除也。

translations.literal: Constantly trembling with fear, never forgetting caution and dread—thereby wishing to prolong Heaven's blessing forever, lest they become those swept aside for later worthies.
translations.idiomatic: They trembled with vigilance to preserve Heaven's favor and avoid becoming stepping-stones for later sages.

sentences.zh: 且臣聞之，懼危者，常安者也；

translations.literal: Moreover I have heard: those who fear peril are often secure.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that those who fear danger tend to stay safe.

sentences.zh: 憂亡者，恆存者也。

translations.literal: Those who worry about perishing are often preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Those who dread ruin tend to endure.

sentences.zh: 使夫有國之君能安不忘危，則本枝百世，長保榮祚，名位與天地無窮，亦何慮乎為來者之驅除哉！

translations.literal: If rulers of states can be secure yet not forget peril, then root and branches endure a hundred generations, long preserve glory and fortune, name and station endless as Heaven and Earth—why fear becoming clearing-houses for those who come after!
translations.idiomatic: If a sovereign rests secure yet remembers peril, the dynasty lasts, honor holds, and standing matches Heaven and Earth—why dread paving the way for successors!

sentences.zh: 傳有之曰：「狂夫之言，明主察焉。」

translations.literal: The tradition has it: "The madman's words—the enlightened ruler examines them."
translations.idiomatic: The classic says: "Even a madman's words deserve the wise ruler's scrutiny."

sentences.zh: 其二曰：士之立業，行非一概。

translations.literal: The second says: In scholars establishing a career, conduct is not of one mold.
translations.idiomatic: The second point: men build careers along paths that differ.

sentences.zh: 吳起貪官，母死不歸，殺妻求將，不孝之甚。

translations.literal: Wu Qi was greedy for office; his mother died and he did not return; he killed his wife to become general—the utmost unfilial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Qi chased rank, skipped his mother's funeral, and slew his wife for a command—utter filial failure.

sentences.zh: 然在魏，使秦人不敢東向；

translations.literal: Yet in Wei he made the Qin people not dare face east.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei he kept Qin from turning eastward.

sentences.zh: 在楚，則三晉不敢南謀。

translations.literal: In Chu then the three Jins did not dare plot southward.
translations.idiomatic: In Chu he stopped the three Jin states from plotting south.

sentences.zh: 曾參、閔騫，誠孝子也，不能宿夕離其親，豈肯出身致死，涉危險之地哉！

translations.literal: Zeng Shen and Min Qian were true filial sons; they could not leave their parents overnight—how could they venture forth to die and tread perilous places!
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Shen and Min Qian were dutiful sons who would not leave parents for a night—how could they risk death in battle!

sentences.zh: 今大晉應期運之所授，齊聖美于有虞，而吳人不臣，稱帝私附，此亦國之羞也。

translations.literal: Now Great Jin received what the age ordained; its sage perfection rivals Shun's; yet Wu men do not submit as subjects and privately adhere to a self-styled emperor—this too is the state's shame.
translations.idiomatic: Great Jin holds Heaven's mandate and virtue rivaling Shun's, yet Wu refuses allegiance and backs a rival emperor—a national shame.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠欲致熊羆之士，不二心之臣，使奮威淮浦、震服蠻荊者，故宜疇咨博采，廣開貢士之路，薦岩穴，舉賢才，征命考試，匪俊莫用。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly desires fierce warriors and ministers of single-minded loyalty to spread awe along the Huai and awe the southern tribes, you ought therefore to consult widely, open broad roads for presenting scholars, recommend men from mountain caves, raise worthy talent, summon and examine them, and employ none who are not outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: If you want stalwart fighters and loyal ministers to awe the Huai region and the south, consult broadly, widen recruitment, lift hidden talent, test candidates, and appoint only the excellent.

sentences.zh: 今台閣選舉，塗塞耳目，九品訪人，唯問中正。

translations.literal: Now terrace-and-pavilion selection blocks ears and eyes; the nine-ranks inquiry asks only the impartial-and-middle.
translations.idiomatic: Palace appointments now blind and deafen policy; the nine-rank system asks only the regional graders.

sentences.zh: 故據上品者，非公侯之子孫，則當塗之昆弟也。

translations.literal: Therefore those occupying upper ranks are either not descendants of dukes and marquises or brothers of those in power.
translations.idiomatic: Hence top ranks go to noble heirs or kin of the powerful.

sentences.zh: 二者苟然，則蓽門蓬戶之俊，安得不有陸沈者哉！

translations.literal: If both are thus, how can talented men from humble gates avoid sinking unnoticed!
translations.idiomatic: If so, how can gifted men of modest birth avoid obscurity!

sentences.zh: 其三曰：昔田子方養老馬，而窮士知所歸，況居天下之廣居，立天下之正位，行天下之大道乎！

translations.literal: The third says: Formerly Tian Zifang cared for old horses, and poor scholars knew where to turn—how much more one who dwells in the world's broad house, stands in the world's correct station, walks the world's great road!
translations.idiomatic: The third point: Tian Zifang fed worn-out horses and men of humble ambition knew whom to follow—how much more should one who holds the broad seat of rule!

sentences.zh: 昔明王聖主，無不養老。

translations.literal: Formerly enlightened kings and sage lords—none failed to care for the aged.
translations.idiomatic: Sage kings of old all honored the elderly.

sentences.zh: 老人眾多，未必皆賢，不可悉養。

translations.literal: The aged are many; they are not necessarily all worthy; one cannot support them all.
translations.idiomatic: Many are old; not all are worthy; the state cannot sustain every elder.

sentences.zh: 故父事三老，所以明孝；

translations.literal: Therefore serving the Three Elders as fathers clarifies filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Honoring the Three Elders as fathers exemplifies filial duty.

sentences.zh: 宗事五更，所以明敬。

translations.literal: Honoring the Five Renewed as ancestors clarifies reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving the Five Geng as seniors exemplifies respect.

sentences.zh: 孟子曰：「吾老以及人之老，吾幼以及人之幼。

translations.literal: Mencius said: "Treat my aged as I treat my aged; treat my young as I treat my young."
translations.idiomatic: Mencius said: "Extend care for your elders to others' elders; extend care for your children to others' children."

sentences.zh: 」今天下雖定，而華山之陽無放馬之群，桃林之下未有休息之牛，故以吳人尚未臣服故也。

translations.literal: Though all under Heaven is now settled, south of Mount Hua there are no herds of released horses; beneath Peach Grove no resting oxen—because Wu men have not yet submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Though the realm is pacified, there are no demobilized herds south of Mount Hua or rested oxen under Peach Grove—because Wu still resists.

sentences.zh: 夫饑者易為食，渴者易為飲，天下元元瞻望新政。

translations.literal: The hungry easily accept food; the thirsty easily accept drink; the common people gaze toward the new policies.
translations.idiomatic: The starving welcome any meal; the thirsty any drink; the people watch for humane rule.

sentences.zh: 願陛下思子方之仁，念犬馬之勞，思帷蓋之報，發仁惠之詔，廣開養老之制。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to ponder Zifang's kindness, remember the labor of dogs and horses, reflect on repaying carriage-and-awning kindness, issue humane and gracious edicts, and broadly open a system for caring for the aged.
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to recall Tian Zifang's compassion, repay loyal service, honor old obligations, issue gracious decrees, and institute broad care for the aged.

sentences.zh: 其四曰：法令賞罰，莫大乎信。

translations.literal: The fourth says: In laws, commands, rewards, and punishments, nothing is greater than trustworthiness.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth point: laws and sanctions hinge above all on good faith.

sentences.zh: 古人有言：「人而無信，不知其可。

translations.literal: The ancients said: "If a man lacks trustworthiness, I do not know how he can stand."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: "Without trustworthiness, a man is good for nothing."

sentences.zh: 」況有養人以惠，使人以義，而可以不信行之哉！

translations.literal: How much more when nourishing others with kindness and employing others with rightness—can one carry this out without trust!
translations.idiomatic: How much less can one rule others by kindness and duty without keeping one's word!

sentences.zh: 臣前為西郡太守，被州所下《己未詔書》：「羌胡道遠，其但募取樂行，不樂勿強。

translations.literal: Your servant formerly was governor of the western commandery and received from the province the "Jiwei Edict": "The Qiang and Hu are far away; only enlist those glad to go—do not force the unwilling."
translations.idiomatic: As governor of the western commandery I received the provincial "Jiwei Edict": enlist Qiang and Hu only if willing—never coerce.

sentences.zh: 」臣被詔書，輒宣恩廣募，示以賞信，所得人名即條言征西。

translations.literal: Your servant received the edict and then spread grace and broadly recruited, showed them rewards would be kept, and listed each man's name to report to the west-campaign authority.
translations.idiomatic: I announced the policy, recruited widely, promised reliable rewards, and forwarded each volunteer's name to the western campaign staff.

sentences.zh: 其晉人自可差簡丁強，如法調取；

translations.literal: Jin people themselves could be drafted by selecting adult males according to statute.
translations.idiomatic: Jin subjects could be levied by drafting able-bodied men under statute.

sentences.zh: 至於羌胡，非恩意告諭，則無欲度金城、河西者也。

translations.literal: As for Qiang and Hu, unless kindness and intent were declared in instructions, none wished to cross Mount Jincheng and west of the River.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang and Hu would not cross Jincheng or the western frontier unless persuaded by fair notice and kindness.

sentences.zh: 自往每興軍渡河，未曾有變，故刺史郭綏勸帥有方，深加獎厲，要許重報。

translations.literal: Formerly whenever armies rose and crossed the River, there had never been trouble; therefore Inspector Guo Sui, skilled at encouraging commanders, was deeply rewarded and promised heavy repayment.
translations.idiomatic: Past campaigns across the river brought no mutiny; Inspector Guo Sui led well and earned rich promises of reward.

sentences.zh: 是以所募感恩利賞，遂立績效，功在第一。

translations.literal: Thus those enlisted, grateful for profit and reward, then achieved merit; their achievement ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: Volunteers, trusting pay and honors, fought hard and topped the merit rolls.

sentences.zh: 今州郡督將，並已受封，羌胡健兒，或王或侯，不蒙論敘也。

translations.literal: Now provincial governors and military overseers have all received enfeoffment; stalwart Qiang and Hu warriors—some kings, some marquises—receive no accounting of their merits.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now prefects and generals are ennobled while Qiang and Hu fighters—some already titled king or marquis—go unrecognized.

sentences.zh: 晉文猶不貪原而失信，齊桓不惜地而背盟，況聖主乎！

translations.literal: Duke Wen of Jin still did not covet Yuan and break trust; Duke Huan of Qi did not spare territory and betray covenant—how much more a sage lord!
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen refused to seize Yuanyi at the cost of his word; Duke Huan would not break alliance for land—how much more should a sage ruler!

sentences.zh: 其五曰：昔周、漢之興，樹親建德，周因五等之爵，漢有河山之誓。

translations.literal: The fifth says: Formerly Zhou and Han at their rise planted kin and established virtue; Zhou relied on five-grade nobility; Han had its oath by rivers and mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth point: Zhou and Han at their founding enfeoffed kin and built virtue—Zhou through five noble ranks, Han through oaths tying house to realm.

sentences.zh: 及其衰也，神器奪於重臣，國祚移於他人。

translations.literal: When they declined, the sacred regalia was seized by mighty ministers and the dynastic fortune shifted to others.
translations.idiomatic: In decline the imperial insignia passed to powerful ministers and the mandate shifted away.

sentences.zh: 故滅周者秦，非姬姓也；

translations.literal: Therefore Zhou's destroyer was Qin, not the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Qin ended Zhou, not another Ji prince.

sentences.zh: 代漢者魏，非劉氏也。

translations.literal: Han's successor was Wei, not the Liu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei succeeded Han, not another Liu.

sentences.zh: 於今國家大計，使異姓無裂土專封之邑，同姓並據有連城之地，縱復令諸王後世子孫還自相並，蓋亦楚人失繁弱於雲夢，尚未為亡其弓也。

translations.literal: As for today's great state plan: let unrelated surnames have no fiefs with sole carved-out authority; let imperial clansmen together hold lands of linked cities; even if later generations of kings gradually annex one another in turn, it is still like Chu losing the Fanruo bow in Yunmeng—not yet to count as losing one's bow.
translations.idiomatic: Today's policy bars outsiders from autonomous bases while princes hold contiguous domains; even if later princes consume one another, it remains like the Chu tale of dropping a prized bow in Yunmeng—the founding house still owns the bow.

sentences.zh: 其於神器不移他族，則始祖不遷之廟，萬年億兆不改其名矣。

translations.literal: As for the sacred regalia not shifting to another clan, then the founding ancestor's unmoved temple and the myriad ages' name would never change.
translations.idiomatic: So long as the imperial token stays in the founding line, the first emperor's temple and dynastic title endure unchanged.

sentences.zh: 大晉諸王二十餘人，而公侯伯子男五百餘國，欲言其國皆小乎，則漢祖之起，俱無尺土之地，況有國者哉！

translations.literal: Great Jin has more than twenty kings and over five hundred states of dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons—if one says their states are all small, Han's ancestor rose with not an inch of ground when all held states!
translations.idiomatic: Jin lists twenty-odd princes and five hundred-odd noble domains—yet size is no proof of weakness: Han's founder began landless while rivals held states.

sentences.zh: 將謂大晉世世賢聖，而諸侯之胤常不肖邪，則放勳欽明而有丹硃，瞽瞍頑凶面虞舜。

translations.literal: Or shall we say Great Jin will be sage generation after generation while feudal heirs are always unworthy—yet Yao was enlightened yet had Dan Zhu; Gu Sou was stubborn and vicious yet fathered Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Will every Jin ruler be sage and every cadet line worthless? Yao sired Dan Zhu; the blind Gu Sou fathered Shun.

sentences.zh: 天下有事無不由兵，而無故多樹兵本，廣開亂原，臣故曰五等不便也。

translations.literal: Whenever there is trouble under Heaven it never bypasses arms; yet without cause planting many roots of arms and broadly opening sources of chaos—your servant therefore says the five grades are inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: Crisis always involves armies; to multiply military bases and invite chaos without cause is why I reject the five-rank enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 臣以為可如前表，諸王宜大其國，增益其兵，悉遣守籓，使形勢足以相接，則陛下可高枕而臥耳。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks one may follow the prior memorial: kings ought to enlarge their states, increase their troops, all be sent to guard their screens until their strategic positions can mutually link—then Your Majesty may sleep with pillow high.
translations.idiomatic: I urge adopting my earlier proposal: enlarge princely domains and armies, post them on frontier defense until their positions link—then you may rest easy.

sentences.zh: 臣以為諸侯伯子男名號皆宜改易之，使封爵之制，祿奉禮秩，並同天下諸侯之例。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks the titles of feudal dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons ought all be altered so that enfeoffment regulations, salary stipends, ritual ranks accord uniformly with the exemplar of all-under-Heaven feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: I would rename duke-through-baron ranks so salaries, ritual precedence, and enfeoffment rules match those of regional lords empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 臣聞與覆車同軌者未嘗安也，與死人同病者未嘗生也，與亡國同法者未嘗存也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that those who ride the same track as an overturned cart have never been secure; those who share the same sickness as the dead have never lived; those who share the same laws as a perished state have never survived.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard: share the rut of an overturned cart and you will not stay safe; share the ailment of the dead and you will not live; copy a fallen state's laws and you will not endure.

sentences.zh: 況夫巍巍大晉，方將登太山，禪梁父，刻石書勳，垂示無窮。

translations.literal: How much more when lofty Great Jin is about to ascend Mount Tai, perform the Liangfu sacrifice, carve stone and record merit, displaying endless glory.
translations.idiomatic: How much more as lofty Jin prepares Taishan rites, Liangfu sacrifice, stone tablets and lasting fame.

sentences.zh: 宜遠鑒往代興廢，深為嚴防，使著事奮筆，必有紀焉。

translations.literal: One ought to mirror distant generations' rise and fall, guard strictly deep within, so that when compilers take up brush there will surely be record.
translations.idiomatic: Study past rises and falls, guard within with rigor, so historians who write will have deeds worth recording.

sentences.zh: 昔伊尹恥其君不為堯、舜，此臣所以私懷慷慨，自忘輕賤者也。

translations.literal: Formerly Yi Yin was ashamed his lord was not Yao or Shun—this is why your servant privately harbors fervor and forgets his lowliness.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Yin was ashamed his ruler fell short of Yao and Shun—hence my earnest zeal despite my humble station.

sentences.zh: 灼書奏，帝覽而異焉，擢為明威將軍、魏興太守。

translations.literal: When Duan Zhuo's memorial was submitted, the emperor read it and marveled; he promoted him to General Who Displays Might and governor of Weixing.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Zhuo submitted his memorial, the emperor read it with admiration and promoted him to General Who Inspires Awe and prefect of Weixing.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He ended life in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died while still holding his appointment.

sentences.zh: 閻纘，字續伯，巴西安漢人也。

translations.literal: Yan Zuan, courtesy Xubo, was a man of Anhan in Baxi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zuan, courtesy name Xubo, came from Anhan in Baxi.

sentences.zh: 祖圃，為張魯功曹，勸魯降魏，封平樂鄉侯。

translations.literal: His grandfather Pu served Zhang Lu as officer of merit, urged Lu to surrender to Wei, and was enfeoffed as village marquis of Pingle.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan Pu had been officer of merit under Zhang Lu, urged surrender to Wei, and received the village marquisate of Pingle.

sentences.zh: 父璞，嗣爵，仕吳至牂柯太守。

translations.literal: Father Pu inherited the title; he served Wu and rose to Administrator of Zangke.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan Pu inherited the fief and served Wu, reaching the post of Administrator of Zangke.

sentences.zh: 纘僑居河南新安，少游英豪，多所交結，博覽墳典，該通物理。

translations.literal: Zuan lived as a sojourner south of the river in Xin'an of Henan; in youth he mingled with heroes and bold spirits, formed many ties, read widely in the canonical writings, and mastered natural principle.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan had settled south of the Yellow River at Xin'an in Henan; as a young man he moved among spirited men of enterprise, formed many connections, read broadly in the classics, and gained a thorough grasp of how things work.

sentences.zh: 父卒，繼母不慈，纘恭事彌謹。

translations.literal: When his father died, his stepmother was unkind; Zuan served her with ever greater reverence.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death his stepmother treated him harshly; Zuan showed her still more deferential respect.

sentences.zh: 而母疾之愈甚，乃誣纘盜父時金寶，訟於有司。

translations.literal: Yet she bore him greater malice and falsely accused Zuan of stealing gems and treasures his father had left, filing suit with the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Her resentment only grew; she falsely charged Zuan with stealing his father's jewels and treasures and brought the case before officials.

sentences.zh: 遂被清議十餘年，纘無怨色，孝謹不怠。

translations.literal: Thus he endured pure criticism for more than ten years; Zuan showed no resentment and never slackened in filial duty or careful conduct.
translations.idiomatic: For over ten years he labored under harsh moral censure; Zuan betrayed no bitterness and never relaxed his filial attentions.

sentences.zh: 母后意解，更移中正，乃得復品。

translations.literal: Later his mother's feelings eased; his regional grading officer was replaced, and he regained his rank evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: When his stepmother relented and his provincial registrar was changed, he could again receive a proper nine-rank rating.

sentences.zh: 為太傅楊駿舍人，轉安復令。

translations.literal: He served as retainer to Grand Tutor Yang Jun, then was transferred to magistrate of Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: He became a house official under Grand Tutor Yang Jun and later was appointed magistrate of Anfu.

sentences.zh: 駿之誅也，纘棄官歸，要駿故主簿潘岳、掾崔基等共葬之。

translations.literal: When Yang Jun was executed, Zuan quit office and returned home; he called on Yang Jun's former chief clerk Pan Yue, aide Cui Ji, and others to bury him together.
translations.idiomatic: At Yang Jun's execution Zuan resigned and went home; he insisted that Yang's former chief clerk Pan Yue, clerk Cui Ji, and others join him in giving Yang a burial.

sentences.zh: 基、嶽畏罪，推纘為主。

translations.literal: Ji and Yue feared punishment and pressed Zuan to take the lead.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing legal consequences, Cui and Pan pushed Zuan to head the affair.

sentences.zh: 墓成，當葬，駿從弟模告武陵王澹，將表殺造意者。

translations.literal: When the tomb was finished and burial was due, Yang Jun's cousin Yang Mo informed Prince Wuling Sima Dan, who intended to memorialize for executing those who had conceived the plan.
translations.idiomatic: As the grave neared completion and the funeral approached, Yang Jun's cousin Yang Mo reported to Prince Sima Dan of Wuling, who planned to memorialize that the ringleaders be put to death.

sentences.zh: 眾咸懼，填塚而逃，纘獨以家財成墓，葬駿而去。

translations.literal: All were terrified; they abandoned the mound and fled; Zuan alone spent family wealth to finish the tomb, buried Yang Jun, and left.
translations.idiomatic: The company panicked, fled, and left the burial unfinished; Zuan alone drew on his family's means to complete the grave, inter Yang Jun, and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒鄒湛以纘才堪佐著作，薦于秘書監華嶠。

translations.literal: Libationer of the Imperial Academy Zou Zhan, deeming Zuan fit to assist compilation work, recommended him to Palace Secretary Hua Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Zhan, libationer of the national university, judged Zuan capable of assisting editorial duty and recommended him to Palace Secretary Hua Qiao.

sentences.zh: 嶠曰：「此職閑廩重，貴勢多爭之，不暇求其才。

translations.literal: Qiao said: "That post is idle yet its salary is heavy; men of rank and power contend for it endlessly; there is no room to seek real talent."
translations.idiomatic: Hua Qiao replied: "That office is a soft berth with a fat stipend; powerful families fight over it without rest; nobody has leisure to consider genuine ability."

sentences.zh: 」遂不能用。

translations.literal: So he was not employed.
translations.idiomatic: The recommendation went nowhere.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒引為西戎校尉司馬，有功，封平樂鄉侯。

translations.literal: Prince Hejian Sima Yong appointed him marshal of the Colonel of the Western Rong; he earned merit and was enfeoffed Marquis of Pingle Township.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Yong of Hejian brought him in as marshal on the staff of the Colonel of the Western Barbarians; for merit he was enfeoffed as village marquis of Pingle.

sentences.zh: 湣懷太子之廢也，纘輿棺詣闕，上書理太子之冤曰：

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Sima Yu was deposed, Zuan drove a hearse to the palace gate and submitted a memorial arguing the crown prince's injustice, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Minhuai Sima Yu was removed, Zuan took a bier to the palace gates and presented a memorial protesting the injustice, declaring:

sentences.zh: 伏見赦文及榜下前太子遹手疏，以為驚愕。

translations.literal: "Your servant has seen in the amnesty text and in Crown Prince Yu's handwritten submission posted beneath the placard; I am struck with dismay."
translations.idiomatic: "I have read the amnesty edict and the memorial in the former heir's own hand that was posted under the board; I am stunned."

sentences.zh: 自古以來，臣子悖逆，未有如此之甚也。

translations.literal: "Never since antiquity has subject or son been rebellious to this degree."
translations.idiomatic: "In all recorded time no minister or son has turned against his lord or father with such violence."

sentences.zh: 幸賴天慈，全其首領。

translations.literal: "Fortunately Heaven's mercy spared his life."
translations.idiomatic: "We are fortunate that Heaven's kindness left him his head."

sentences.zh: 臣伏念遹生於聖父而至此者，由於長養深宮，沈淪富貴，受饒先帝，父母驕之。

translations.literal: "Your servant reflects that Yu was born of a sage father yet reached this pass because he was reared deep in the palace, sunk in wealth and honor, favored by the late emperor, and indulged by father and mother."
translations.idiomatic: "I reflect that Yu had a sage for a father yet came to this because he was raised behind palace walls, drowned in luxury, spoiled by the late emperor, and pampered by his parents."

sentences.zh: 每見選師傅下至群吏，率取膏粱擊鐘鼎食之家，稀有寒門儒素如衛綰、周文、石奮、疏廣，洗馬、舍人亦無汲黯、鄭莊之比，遂使不見事父事君之道。

translations.literal: "Whenever tutors were chosen down to the clerks, they were almost always from houses that dine on fine grain and strike bells at meals; rarely did poor scholars such as Wei Wan, Zhou Wen, Shi Fen, and Shu Guang appear; among gentlemen stewards and retainers none matched Ji An or Zheng Zhuang - so he never learned how to serve a father or serve a lord."
translations.idiomatic: "Those appointed tutors and clerks were invariably sons of the wealthy and powerful; one seldom saw humble scholars like Wei Wan, Zhou Wen, Shi Fen, or Shu Guang; among stewards of the heir there were none to rival Ji An or Zheng Zhuang - so he never learned how to honor a father or serve a sovereign."

sentences.zh: 臣案古典，太子居以士禮，與國人齒，以此明先王欲令知先賤然後乃貴。

translations.literal: "Your servant consults classical models: the crown prince dwells by rites due a scholar and ranks with the common people - whereby former kings meant him to know lowliness before nobility."
translations.idiomatic: "The classics teach that an heir should live by the etiquette of a gentleman and stand among ordinary folk - so that kings of old meant him to learn humility before greatness."

sentences.zh: 自頃東宮亦微太盛，所以致敗也。

translations.literal: "Of late the Eastern Palace too verged on excess; that is why ruin followed."
translations.idiomatic: "Recently the heir's establishment itself bordered on extravagance; that is how it came to grief."

sentences.zh: 非但東宮，曆觀諸王師友文學，皆豪族力能得者，率非龔遂、王陽，能以道訓。

translations.literal: "Nor is it only the Eastern Palace: surveying princes' tutors, friends, and literary attendants, they are almost always men powerful houses could secure - hardly ever Gong Sui or Wang Yang able to instruct by the Way."
translations.idiomatic: "Nor is this confined to the Eastern Palace: look at tutors, companions, and literary aides for any prince - they are nearly always placements secured by great clans; one rarely finds moral teachers like Gong Sui or Wang Yang."

sentences.zh: 友無亮直三益之節，官以文學為名，實不讀書，但共鮮衣好馬，縱酒高會，嬉遊博弈，豈有切磋，能相長益！

translations.literal: "Friends lack the integrity of the three beneficial companionships; offices titled literary in fact never read - they only share bright clothes and fine horses, pour wine at lofty gatherings, roam and gamble; where is polish or mutual improvement?"
translations.idiomatic: "Companions lack the steadfast honesty of truly helpful friendship; posts labeled 'literary' involve no real study - only fine dress, fast horses, drinking parties, outings, and games; nothing remotely like earnest mutual refinement happens."

sentences.zh: 臣常恐公族遲陵，以此歎息。

translations.literal: "Your servant has often feared decline among the ducal houses and sighed for this."
translations.idiomatic: "I have long worried that the imperial kin would slip into decay and have mourned it."

sentences.zh: 今遹可以為戒，恐其被斥，棄逐遠郊，始當悔過，無所復及。

translations.literal: "Now Yu may serve as a warning; I fear that once cast off and driven to distant outskirts he will repent - too late to mend."
translations.idiomatic: "Let Yu be a lesson; I fear that once he is rejected and banished to remote borders he will regret his faults when nothing can be done."

sentences.zh: 昔戾太子無狀，稱兵距命，而壺關三老上書，有田千秋之言，猶曰：「子弄父兵，罪應笞耳！

translations.literal: Formerly Crown Prince Li behaved outrageously, raised arms and resisted his father's command; yet the Huguan elder submitted a memorial, and Tian Qianqiu's words ran: "A son played with his father's troops - the punishment should be a flogging!"
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Liu Ju acted rashly and took up arms against his father's orders, the elder of Huguan still petitioned the throne, and Tian Qianqiu's argument held that 'a son who borrows his father's soldiers deserves no more than a beating.'

sentences.zh: 」漢武感悟之，築思子之台。

translations.literal: Han Wudi took it to heart and built the Terrace of Longing for a Son.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, Emperor Wu built the Terrace where he could mourn his son.

sentences.zh: 今遹無狀，言語悖逆，受罪之日，不敢失道，猶為輕于戾太子，尚可禁持，重選保傅。

translations.literal: Now Yu's misconduct - insolent words - is lighter than Crown Prince Li's; on the day he suffered punishment he did not stray from duty; he may still be restrained and given newly chosen tutors and guardians.
translations.idiomatic: Yu has misbehaved with rash speech, yet his offense is lighter than Liu Ju's; even under punishment he did not bolt from proper deportment; he can still be kept under close discipline with new tutors and guardians.

sentences.zh: 如司空張華，道德深遠，乃心忠誠，以為之師。

translations.literal: Take Minister of Works Zhang Hua, whose virtue runs deep and whose heart is loyal - assign him tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Zhang Hua combines profound moral stature with steadfast loyalty - make him senior tutor.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫劉寔，寒苦自立，終始不衰，年同呂望，經藉不廢，以為之保。

translations.literal: Take Imperial Household Grandee Liu Shi, who rose from hardship and never flagged, old as Lu Wang, never abandoning the classics - assign him guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Household Grandee Liu Shi endured poverty yet held firm through life; though aged like Jiang Taigong he never set his studies aside - make him guardian.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射裴頠，明允恭肅，體道居正，以為之友。

translations.literal: Take Vice Director of the Secretariat Pei Wei, discerning, trustworthy, reverent, embodying the Way and holding to rectitude - assign him friend.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Secretariat Pei Wei is lucid, trustworthy, and grave; he embodies the Way and keeps to what is right - make him companion.

sentences.zh: 置游談文學，皆選寒門孤宦以學行自立者，及取服勤更事、涉履艱難、事君事親、名行素聞者，使與共處。

translations.literal: For roaming companions and literary attendants, choose men from poor gates and solitary offices who established themselves by learning and conduct, and men seasoned in hardship who are known for serving lord and parent - let them dwell with him.
translations.idiomatic: Pick wandering companions and literary aides from humble families and lonely posts - men who made their names through scholarship and character - and veterans tempered by hardship with reputations for serving sovereign and kin; house them with the heir.

sentences.zh: 使嚴御史監護其家，絕貴戚子弟、輕薄賓客。

translations.literal: Assign stern censors to oversee his household and shut out noble youths and frivolous guests.
translations.idiomatic: Station rigorous censors over his establishment and bar noble wastrels and flashy hangers-on.

sentences.zh: 如此，左右前後，莫非正人。

translations.literal: Thus to left and right, before and behind, none will not be upright men.
translations.idiomatic: Then everyone around him - every quarter - will be honorable men.

sentences.zh: 師傅文學，可令十日一講，使共論議於前。

translations.literal: Tutors, guardians, and literary attendants may lecture once every ten days and debate together in his presence.
translations.idiomatic: Have tutors, guardians, and literary aides lecture every tenth day and dispute doctrine before him.

sentences.zh: 敕使但道古今孝子慈親，忠臣事君，及思愆改過之義，皆聞善道，庶幾可全。

translations.literal: Order them only to speak of filial sons cherishing parents and loyal ministers serving their lord, and of acknowledging fault and reform - let him hear the good Way; perhaps he may be preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: Instruct them to discourse on dutiful sons, faithful ministers, admitting errors and mending ways - so he hears what is right and may yet be saved intact.

sentences.zh: 昔太甲有罪，放之三年，思庸克復，為殷明王。

translations.literal: Formerly Taijia offended and was banished three years; reflecting on constant renewal he became an enlightened king of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: King Taijia erred and spent three years in exile; once he embraced renewal he became a worthy ruler of Shang.

sentences.zh: 又魏文帝懼於見廢，夙夜自祗，竟能自全。

translations.literal: Again Wei Wendi feared deposition and strove day and night in self-discipline; in the end he saved himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wendi lived in dread of being cast aside and disciplined himself ceaselessly; he survived.

sentences.zh: 及至明帝，因母得罪，廢為平原侯，為置家臣庶子，師友文學，皆取正人，共相匡矯。

translations.literal: When it came to Mingdi, because his mother incurred guilt he was demoted to Marquis of Pingyuan; household ministers, junior sons, tutors, friends, and literary attendants were all chosen from upright men who jointly corrected him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingdi, whose mother had fallen under suspicion, the prince was reduced to Marquis of Pingyuan; ministers of his household, tutors, companions, and literary aides were all upright men who worked together to straighten him out.

sentences.zh: 兢兢慎罰，事父以孝，父沒，事母以謹，聞于天下，於今稱之。

translations.literal: Fearful and careful under punishment, he served his father with filial piety; when his father died he served his mother with scruple - his fame reached the realm and is praised to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Chastened and cautious, he honored his father filially; after his father's death he tended his mother with meticulous care - his virtue became known across the realm and is honored still.

sentences.zh: 漢高皇帝數置酒於庭，欲廢太子，後四皓為師，子房為傅，竟復成就。

translations.literal: The Han Founder repeatedly held wine feasts in the hall intending to replace the crown prince; later the Four Hoary Heads became tutors and Zifang guardian - at last the heir was secured.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu often banqueted in the palace intending to change heirs; only when the Four Elders became tutors and Zhang Liang guardian was the succession stabilized.

sentences.zh: 前事不忘，後事之戒。

translations.literal: Not forgetting past affairs is the lesson for those to come.
translations.idiomatic: Heeding earlier mistakes prevents later disaster.

sentences.zh: 孟軻有雲，「孤臣孽子，其操心也危，慮患也深」，故多善功。

translations.literal: Meng Ke said: "Orphaned ministers and sons of concubines worry at heart and ponder peril deeply" - so they often achieve good deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius observed that 'ministers out of favor and sons born to secondary wives live on edge and think hard about danger' - which is why they often accomplish something worthy.

sentences.zh: 李斯云：「慈母多敗子，嚴家無格虜。

translations.literal: Li Si said: "Tender mothers ruin many sons; strict households have no shackled captives."
translations.idiomatic: Li Si wrote that 'doting mothers spoil children; disciplined households produce no chained prisoners.'

sentences.zh: 」由陛下驕遹使至於此，庶其受罪以來，足自思改。

translations.literal: "Because Your Majesty indulged Yu until this came to pass - perhaps since his punishment he has had enough to reflect and reform."
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty's indulgence brought Yu to this; perhaps suffering punishment has taught him to reconsider and reform."

sentences.zh: 方今天下多虞，四夷未寧，將伺國隙。

translations.literal: Today the realm is full of troubles; the four barbarians are not yet settled and watch for openings in the state.
translations.idiomatic: The empire is beset with alarms; border peoples are restless and wait for domestic weakness.

sentences.zh: 儲副大事，不宜空虛。

translations.literal: The heir-apparent is a great matter; the position ought not stand empty.
translations.idiomatic: The succession is too important to leave vacant.

sentences.zh: 宜為大計，小復停留。

translations.literal: You should plan for the long term and pause a little longer.
translations.idiomatic: Think of the grand design and defer final judgment awhile.

sentences.zh: 先加嚴誨。

translations.literal: First apply stern admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Begin with rigorous instruction.

sentences.zh: 依平原侯故事，若不悛改，棄之未晚也。

translations.literal: Follow the precedent of the Marquis of Pingyuan; if he does not repent and amend, casting him off will not yet be late.
translations.idiomatic: Treat him as Cao Rui was treated when demoted to Marquis of Pingyuan; if he still refuses to mend his ways, disinheriting him will not be too late.

sentences.zh: 臣素寒門，無力仕宦，不經東宮，情不私遹。

translations.literal: Your servant comes from a humble gate with no influence for office; I never served the Eastern Palace - my feelings do not privately favor Yu.
translations.idiomatic: I am from a poor house without connections for advancement; I never held office in the heir's establishment - I have no private stake in Yu.

sentences.zh: 念昔楚國處女諫其王曰「有龍無尾」，言年四十，未有太子。

translations.literal: I recall how a maiden of Chu remonstrated with her king, saying "There is a dragon without a tail" - meaning he was forty and still had no crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: I remember the Chu maiden who warned her king of 'a dragon without a tail' - that at forty he still lacked an heir.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗備近職，雖未得自結天日，情同閽寺，悾悾之誠，皆為國計。

translations.literal: Your servant once held office nearby; though I could not bind myself to the imperial presence, my devotion matches that of gatekeepers - all my earnest sincerity aims at the state's plans.
translations.idiomatic: Although I once served at court yet never won personal access to Your Majesty, my earnest loyalty matches that of the humblest usher - every word serves the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣老母見臣為表，乃為臣卜卦，云「書禦即死」。

translations.literal: My aged mother, seeing your servant draft this memorial, divined for me and got the line "Submit the memorial and die."
translations.idiomatic: When my elderly mother saw me drafting this memorial she cast yarrow sticks and read the line 'present the petition and perish.'

sentences.zh: 妻子守臣，涕泣見止。

translations.literal: Wife and children held me back, weeping and begging me to stop.
translations.idiomatic: My wife and children clung to me in tears and pleaded that I desist.

sentences.zh: 臣獨以為頻見拔擢，嘗為近職，此恩難忘，何以報德？

translations.literal: Your servant alone thought: I have been repeatedly promoted and once held nearby office - this grace is hard to forget; how repay such virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Yet I reflected that I had been favored with promotion and palace service - grace I cannot forget - how else repay it?

sentences.zh: 唯當陳誠，以死獻忠。

translations.literal: I can only lay bare my loyalty and offer devotion unto death.
translations.idiomatic: I can only speak plainly and pledge my life.

sentences.zh: 輒具棺絮，伏須刑誅。

translations.literal: I therefore prepare coffin and shroud and await execution.
translations.idiomatic: I have therefore fitted out a coffin with winding-sheet and await the executioner's stroke.

sentences.zh: 書禦不省。

translations.literal: The memorial reached the throne but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The throne received the memorial but took no notice.

sentences.zh: 及張華遇害，賈謐被誅，朝野震悚，纘獨撫華屍慟哭曰：「早語君遜位而不肯，今果不免，命也夫！

translations.literal: When Zhang Hua was murdered and Jia Mi executed, court and countryside trembled; Zuan alone stroked Hua's corpse and wept aloud: "I told you long ago to yield rank and you would not - now indeed you could not escape - such is fate!"
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Hua died by violence and Jia Mi was cut down, the whole capital shook; only Zuan clasped Zhang Hua's body and cried, 'I urged you long ago to retire - you refused; now there was no escape - so fate runs.'

sentences.zh: 」過叱賈謐屍曰：「小兒亂國之由，誅其晚矣！」

translations.literal: Passing Jia Mi's corpse he rebuked: "You boy were the cause of the realm's chaos - your execution came late!"
translations.idiomatic: Passing Jia Mi's corpse he shouted, 'You brat brought the dynasty to ruin - justice came too late!'

sentences.zh: 皇太孫立，纘復上疏曰：

translations.literal: When the imperial great-grandson was established, Zuan again submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: When an imperial great-grandson was named heir, Zuan presented another memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣前上書訟太子之枉，不見省覽。

translations.literal: Your servant formerly submitted a memorial pleading the crown prince's wrong and it was not reviewed.
translations.idiomatic: I once petitioned about the crown prince's injustice; it never reached deliberation.

sentences.zh: 昔壺關三老陳衛太子之冤，而漢武築思子之台。

translations.literal: Formerly the Huguan elder stated Crown Prince Wei's grievance and Han Wudi built the Terrace of Longing for a Son.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the Huguan elder aired Crown Prince Wei's wrongs and Emperor Wu raised the Terrace of Longing for a Son.

sentences.zh: 高廟令田千秋上書，不敢正言，托以鬼神之教，而孝武大感，月中三遷，位至丞相，乘車入殿，號曰車氏。

translations.literal: Gaomiao Director Tian Qianqiu submitted a memorial - not daring to speak plainly he appealed through teachings about ghosts and spirits; Xiaowu was deeply moved, thrice promoted him within a month until he reached chancellor, rode a carriage into the hall, and was called the Coachman clan.
translations.idiomatic: Director Tian Qianqiu of Gaodi's shrine submitted a memorial; too timid to speak openly he framed it as a ghost's warning; Emperor Wu was shaken, raised him three ranks within a month to chancellor, allowed him to ride his carriage into the hall, and folk dubbed him the Coachman house.

sentences.zh: 恨臣精誠微薄，不能有感，竟使太子流離，沒命許昌。

translations.literal: I regret that your servant's earnest devotion was slight and could not move authority - so in the end the crown prince was driven about and lost his life at Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: My devotion proved too slight to sway the court - so the heir wandered as an outcast and died at Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 向令陛下即納臣言，不致此禍。

translations.literal: Had Your Majesty then accepted your servant's words, this calamity would not have occurred.
translations.idiomatic: Had Your Majesty heeded me then, this tragedy would not have happened.

sentences.zh: 天贊聖意，三公獻謀，庶人賜死，罪人斯得，太子以明，臣恨其晚，無所復及。

translations.literal: Heaven aided the sacred intent; the Three Dukes offered counsel; the commoner was condemned to death - the guilty were seized, the crown prince's cause made clear; your servant regrets only that it came late - nothing more can be done.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven upheld your purpose; the Three Excellencies advised wisely; the degraded prince met sentence, villains were seized, and the heir's honor was clarified - I rue only that justice came too late to restore him.

sentences.zh: 詔書慈悼，迎喪反葬，復其禮秩，誠副眾望，不意呂、霍之變復生於今日！

translations.literal: The edict showed compassionate grief, welcomed the coffin home for burial, and restored his ritual rank - it truly answered popular expectation; who would have thought the disorders of Lu and Huo should recur today!
translations.idiomatic: Your grieving edict welcomed his coffin home and restored his titles - exactly what people hoped - yet who imagined we would see another Lu-Huo coup today!

sentences.zh: 伏見詔書建立太孫，斯誠陛下上順先典以安社稷，中慰慈悼冤魂之痛，下令萬國心有所系。

translations.literal: Your servant has seen the edict establishing the great-grandson - this truly carries forward the former canons above to steady the altars of soil and grain, midway consoles with compassionate mourning the pain of the wronged soul, and below gives the myriad states something to cling to.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen the edict enthroning the great-grandson - it carries ancient precedent aloft to settle the altars, midway offers sorrowful comfort to the prince unjustly slain, and below gives every province an heir to rally round.

sentences.zh: 追惟庶人，所為無狀，幾傾宗廟，賴相國、太宰至忠憤發，潛謀俱斷，奉贊聖意，以成神武。

translations.literal: Reflecting on the commoner's conduct - beyond all bounds - it nearly overturned the ancestral temple; thanks to the Chancellor of State and Grand Tutor, utmost loyalty blazed forth, hidden plots were severed together, they aided the sacred intent and perfected divine martial prowess.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed prince's plotting nearly destroyed the dynasty; only the sheer loyalty of your Chancellor and Grand Tutor, cutting intrigue short and aiding your resolve, matched Heaven's martial awe.

sentences.zh: 雖周誅二叔，漢掃諸呂，未足以喻。

translations.literal: Though Zhou executed the two uncles and Han swept away the various Lus, it is not enough for comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Even Zhou's execution of the two rebel uncles and Han's purge of the Lu faction hardly surpass this.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下因此大更厘改，以為永制。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty would seize this moment for sweeping reform and make it lasting statute.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to turn this crisis into thorough reform and codify it for the ages.

sentences.zh: 禮置太子，居以士禮，與國人齒，為置官屬，皆如朋友，不為純臣。

translations.literal: By ritual when establishing a crown prince he dwells by rites due a scholar and ranks with the common people; household officials are appointed like friends, not as mere subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Rite prescribes that an heir live as a gentleman among commoners; household officers should relate as friends, not as cringing ministers.

sentences.zh: 既使上厭至望，以崇孝道，又令不相嚴憚，易相規正。

translations.literal: Thus above he satisfies supreme expectation and exalts filial duty; below mutual awe is eased and correction comes easily.
translations.idiomatic: Above you satisfy Heaven's demand and elevate filial piety; below mutual dread softens so frank correction is easier.

sentences.zh: 昔漢武既信奸讒，危害太子，復用望氣之言，欲盡誅詔獄中囚。

translations.literal: Formerly Han Wudi, having trusted slanderous villains and harmed the crown prince, again heeded qi-watching men and wished to execute all prisoners in the imperial jail.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wudi once listened to slander and ruined his heir, then credited omens and meant to slaughter every inmate of the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 邴吉以皇孫在焉，閉門距命，後遂擁護皇孫，督罰乳母，卒至成人，立為孝宣皇帝。

translations.literal: Bing Ji, because the imperial grandson was there, barred the gate and refused the order; later he shielded the imperial grandson, disciplined the wet nurse, and at last brought him to adulthood - he was enthroned as Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Ji, knowing the imperial grandson lay inside, sealed the gates and defied the edict; he guarded the boy, punished a negligent nurse, reared him to manhood, and saw him enthroned as Xuandi.

sentences.zh: 苟志於忠，無往不可。

translations.literal: If the will is set on loyalty, nothing stands in the way.
translations.idiomatic: Where loyalty leads, no obstacle endures.

sentences.zh: 曆觀古人雖不避死，亦由世教寬以成節。

translations.literal: Surveying the ancients, though they did not shrink from death, it was also because the age's teaching was lenient enough to complete their integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The heroes of old faced death boldly, yet their age's customs gave room for heroism to ripen.

sentences.zh: 吉雖距詔書，事在於忠，故宥而不責。

translations.literal: Though Ji resisted the edict, the affair lay in loyalty - so he was pardoned and not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Because Bing Ji's defiance served loyalty, he went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 自晉興已來，用法太嚴，遲速之間，輒加誅斬。

translations.literal: Since Jin arose, law has been applied too harshly; at the slightest delay execution and beheading follow.
translations.idiomatic: Since our dynasty began, justice has grown cruel - hesitate an instant and heads roll.

sentences.zh: 一身伏法，猶可強為，今世之誅，動輒滅門。

translations.literal: One life answering the law might still be borne; today's executions routinely exterminate whole clans.
translations.idiomatic: One man might accept death for his crime; now whole clans perish overnight.

sentences.zh: 昔呂後臨朝，肆意無道。

translations.literal: Formerly Empress Lu held court and wantonly abandoned the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Lu seized power and flouted every moral limit.

sentences.zh: 周昌相趙，三召其王而昌不遣，先征昌入，乃後召王。

translations.literal: Zhou Chang assisted Zhao - three times she summoned its king yet Chang would not send him; first she summoned Chang to enter, then summoned the king.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chang governed Zhao; thrice Empress Lu recalled the prince yet Zhou Chang refused dispatch - she had to summon Zhou Chang himself before she could summon the prince.

sentences.zh: 此由漢制本寬，得使為快。

translations.literal: This came about because Han institutions were fundamentally lenient and allowed such bold action.
translations.idiomatic: Han law was loose enough to permit such fierce integrity.

sentences.zh: 假令如今，呂後必謂昌已反，夷其三族，則誰敢復為殺身成義者哉！

translations.literal: Were it like today, Empress Lu would surely call Chang a rebel and wipe out his three kin - then who would again die to fulfill righteousness!
translations.idiomatic: Under today's code Empress Lu would brand Zhou Chang a traitor and exterminate three generations - who then would die for principle?

sentences.zh: 此法宜改，可使經遠。

translations.literal: This law ought to be revised so it may endure far.
translations.idiomatic: Statutes must change if righteousness is to survive.

sentences.zh: 又漢初廢趙王張敖，其臣貫高謀弑高祖，高祖不誅，以明臣道。

translations.literal: Again at the beginning of Han when King Zhao Zhang Ao was deposed, his minister Guan Gao plotted to murder Gaozu; Gaozu did not execute him - to clarify the duty of a minister.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Han, when King Zhang Ao of Zhao fell, minister Guan Gao schemed against Gaozu; Gaozu spared him - to honor loyal service.

sentences.zh: 田叔、孟舒十人為奴，髡鉗隨王，隱親侍養，故令平安。

translations.literal: Tian Shu, Meng Shu, and ten others became slaves, shaved and collared, followed the king, nursed him in hidden devotion - so he came through safely.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Shu, Meng Shu, and ten companions sold themselves as slaves, shaved and shackled, stuck by their lord in secret until he was safe.

sentences.zh: 向使晉法得容為義，東宮之臣得如周昌，固護太子得如邴吉，距詔不坐，伏死諫爭，則聖意必變，太子以安。

translations.literal: Had Jin law allowed room for righteousness, Eastern Palace ministers could have been like Zhou Chang, firmly guarding the crown prince like Bing Ji, resisting edicts without punishment, dying prone in remonstrance - then the sacred intent would surely have shifted and the crown prince would have been safe.
translations.idiomatic: Had Jin's code tolerated duty as Han's did, Eastern Palace officers might have stood like Zhou Chang, guarded the heir like Bing Ji, defied unlawful orders without reprisal, or lain prone remonstrating until the emperor relented - the prince would have lived.

sentences.zh: 如田叔、孟舒侍從不罪者，則隱親左右，奸凶毒藥無緣得設，太子不夭也。

translations.literal: If attendants like Tian Shu and Meng Shu went unpunished, those nursing him at close hand - how could vicious poison and treachery find a path - the crown prince would not have died young.
translations.idiomatic: If servants like Tian Shu and Meng Shu stayed blameless, loyal hands would nurse him - poison and intrigue could not strike - and the heir would not have died young.

sentences.zh: 臣每責東宮臣故無侍從者，後聞頗有于道路望車拜辭，而有司收付洛陽獄，奏科其罪。

translations.literal: Your servant often blamed former Eastern Palace ministers for having no attendants; later I heard that quite a few bowed farewell beside the road watching the carriage - yet the authorities seized them and sent them to Luoyang jail, memorializing to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: I once faulted former Eastern Palace staff for abandoning their lord; I later learned many bowed beside the road as his cart passed - yet agents arrested them for Luoyang's jail and sought sentences.

sentences.zh: 然臣故莫從，良有以也。

translations.literal: Yet your servant's old colleagues did not follow - there was good reason.
translations.idiomatic: Small wonder my old colleagues dared not follow.

sentences.zh: 又本置三率，盛其兵馬，所以宿衛防虞。

translations.literal: Moreover the Three Guards were originally instituted with strong troops and horses to garrison and guard.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the heir's three guard corps exist precisely to camp troops and mount patrols.

sentences.zh: 而使者卒至，莫有警嚴覆請審者，此由恐畏滅族。

translations.literal: Yet when envoys arrived suddenly none stood alert, sought review, or verified - this stemmed from terror of clan extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when messengers arrived abruptly nobody challenged orders - everyone feared extermination of kin.

sentences.zh: 今皇孫沖幼，去事多故。

translations.literal: Now the imperial grandson is young and times hold many troubles.
translations.idiomatic: The great-grandson is a child and the age is perilous.

sentences.zh: 若有不虞，強臣專制，奸邪矯詐，雖有相國保訓東宮，擁佑之恩同于邴吉，適可使玉體安全，宜開來防，可著於令：自今已後，諸有廢興倉卒，群臣皆得輒嚴，須錄詣殿前，面受口詔，然後為信，得同周昌不遣王節，下聽臣子隱親，得如田叔、孟舒，不加罪責，則永固儲副，以後安嗣之遠慮也。

translations.literal: If unforeseen events arise and a powerful minister monopolizes authority or the wicked forge orders - even with a Chancellor instructing the Eastern Palace and shielding grace matching Bing Ji - that only keeps the jade person safe; you should open precautions for the future and write into ordinance: from now on, whenever deposition or enthronement happens in haste, all ministers may immediately stand guard; records must be brought to the hall steps and oral edicts received face to face - only then are they trusted - allowing the Zhou Chang precedent of not releasing the king's tally, and below letting ministers and sons nurse their lord unpunished like Tian Shu and Meng Shu without penalty - thus securing the heir solidly is far-sighted care for safe succession hereafter.
translations.idiomatic: Should crisis strike - a strong minister seize power or forgers issue commands - even a chancellor mentoring the heir with Bing Ji's devotion guards only the boy's body; you must legislate for the future: whenever succession shifts in panic, every minister may mobilize guards; credentials must be examined on the palace steps and verbal orders heard in person before they bind; emulate Zhou Chang withholding the prince's summons and grant immunity to faithful servants like Tian Shu and Meng Shu - only thus is the succession armor-plated for generations.

sentences.zh: 來事難知，往事可改。

translations.literal: What is to come is hard to know; what is past may still be amended.
translations.idiomatic: Tomorrow remains obscure; yesterday's mistakes can still be repaired.

sentences.zh: 臣前每見詹事裴權用心懇惻，舍人秦戢數上疏啟諫；

translations.literal: Your subject formerly each time saw Household Manager Pei Quan apply mind earnest sympathetic, Gentleman-in-Attendance Qin Ji repeatedly ascend memorial open remonstrate;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I saw Household Manager Pei Quan devote himself with heartfelt earnestness, and Gentleman Qin Ji repeatedly submit memorials of frank remonstrance,

sentences.zh: 而爰倩贈以九列，權有忠意，獨不蒙賞。

translations.literal: Yet Yuan Qian posthumously-gift with Nine Ranks, Quan had loyal intent, alone not receive reward.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qian was granted posthumous enrollment among the Nine Ministers, whereas Quan showed loyal intent yet alone received no recognition.

sentences.zh: 謂宜依倩為比，以寵其魂。

translations.literal: Say fitting according-to Qian take-as precedent, thereby honor his soul.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that Quan should be treated by the same measure, to honor his departed spirit.

sentences.zh: 推尋表疏，如秦戢輩及司隸所奏，諸敢拜辭于道路者，明詔稱揚，使微異於眾，以勸為善，以獎將來也。

translations.literal: Trace-search memorials, like Qin Ji sort and Metropolitan Governor what memorialized, all dare decline appointment at road persons, clear edict praise-display, cause slightly differ from multitude, thereby encourage doing good, thereby reward coming-times also.
translations.idiomatic: Review those petitions: men of Qin Ji's sort and those the Metropolitan Governor reported, anyone bold enough to refuse appointment in public ought to be singled out in an explicit edict, set slightly apart from the crowd, to encourage virtue and hold up a standard for the future.

sentences.zh: 纘又陳：

translations.literal: Zuan again set-forth:
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zuan further submitted:

sentences.zh: 今相國雖已保傅東宮，保其安危。

translations.literal: Now Chancellor-of-State although already tutor-guard Eastern Palace, preserve its safety peril.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Chancellor of State already serves as tutor and guardian of the Eastern Palace and safeguards its fortunes,

sentences.zh: 至於旦夕訓誨，輔導出入，動靜劬勞，宜選寒苦之士，忠貞清正，老而不衰，如城門校尉梁柳、白衣南安硃沖比者，以為師傅。

translations.literal: As-for dawn-dusk instruct-admonish, assist-guide exit-enter, movement-rest toil, fitting select cold-bitter gentlemen, loyal chaste pure upright, old yet not decline, like Colonel-of-Gate Liang Liu, white-clothes Nan'an Zhu Chong compare persons, take-as tutors.
translations.idiomatic: for day-and-night instruction, escorting him in and out, and the daily grind of attendance, you should pick men of humble and arduous background who are loyal, upright, incorrupt, and vigorous in old age, such as Colonel of the Gate Liang Liu or the commoner Zhu Chong of Nan'an, and appoint them tutors.

sentences.zh: 其侍臣以下文武將吏，且勿復取盛戚豪門子弟，若吳太妃家室及賈、郭之黨。

translations.literal: Those attendant ministers below civil military general clerks, temporarily not again take flourishing affinal powerful gate sons-younger, like Consort-Dowager Wu household and Jia Guo factions.
translations.idiomatic: Among attendant ministers and civil and military officers, cease for now recruiting heirs of great affinal clans and magnate houses, such as the household of Consort Dowager Wu or the Jia and Guo factions.

sentences.zh: 如此之輩，生而富溢，無念修己，率多輕薄浮華，相驅放縱，皆非所補益於吾少主者也。

translations.literal: Such sort persons, born then wealth overflow, no thought cultivate self, generally many frivolous flashy, mutually drive reckless indulgence, all not those who supplement benefit to our young lord.
translations.idiomatic: Such people grow up in boundless wealth, spare no thought for self-cultivation, are mostly shallow and ostentatious, and spur one another to license; none would truly profit our young sovereign.

sentences.zh: 皆可擇寒門篤行、學問素士、更履險易、節義足稱者，以備群臣，可輕其禮儀，使與古同，於相切磋為益。

translations.literal: All can select cold-gate steadfast conduct learning inquiry plain gentlemen, further tread peril ease, integrity righteousness sufficient praise persons, thereby complete host ministers, can lighten their ritual observances, cause with antiquity same, at mutually polish-cut as profit.
translations.idiomatic: Choose instead men from cold households with steadfast conduct, solid scholarship, experience of both hardship and ease, and integrity worth praising, to fill out the corps of ministers; ease their ceremonial burdens so they mirror antiquity, which will help mutual refinement.

sentences.zh: 昔魏文帝之在東宮，徐幹、劉楨為友，文學相接之道並如氣類。

translations.literal: Formerly Wei Wendi when at Eastern Palace, Xu Gan Liu Zhen as friends, literary studies mutually-connect way altogether like breath-kind.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Wendi lived in the Eastern Palace, Xu Gan and Liu Zhen were his companions; their literary fellowship matched like temperaments drawn together.

sentences.zh: 吳太子登，顧譚為友，諸葛恪為賓，臥同床帳，行則參乘，交如布衣，相呼以字，此則近代之明比也。

translations.literal: Wu Crown Prince Deng, Gu Tan as friend, Zhuge Ke as guest, lie same bed curtain, walk then shield-companion, dealings like plain cloth, mutually call by courtesy-name, this then recent-age clear parallel.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Crown Prince Sun Deng took Gu Tan as friend and Zhuge Ke as guest; they shared bed-curtains and rode together as shield companion; they dealt as commoners and addressed one another by courtesy name: plain parallels from recent history.

sentences.zh: 天子之子不患不富貴，不患人不敬畏，患於驕盈，不聞其過，不知稼穡之艱難耳。

translations.literal: Son-of-Heaven son not worry not rich noble, not worry men not awe respect, worry at arrogance excess, not hear his faults, not know grain-harvest hardship ear.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's son need not fear lacking wealth or rank, nor lack of awe from others; what he must fear is pride and excess, never hearing of his faults, and ignorance of the hardships of farming.

sentences.zh: 至於甚者，乃不知名六畜，可不勉哉！

translations.literal: Reach extreme ones, then not know names six livestock, can not strive!
translations.idiomatic: In the worst cases he does not even know the names of the six domestic animals; how can diligence be neglected?

sentences.zh: 昔周公親撻伯禽，曹參笞窋二百，聖考慈父皆不傷恩。

translations.literal: Formerly Duke-of-Zhou personally whip Boqin, Cao Shen flog Kui two-hundred, sage-examined kind-father all not harm grace.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou personally whipped Boqin; Cao Shen flogged his son Kui two hundred strokes; saintly fathers and loving fathers alike did not thereby destroy affection.

sentences.zh: 今不忍小相維持，令至闕失頓相罪責，不亦誤哉！

translations.literal: Now not bear small mutually restrain, cause reach fault-loss suddenly mutually blame-punish, not also mistaken!
translations.idiomatic: If one cannot endure modest restraint now and lets faults pile up until blame crashes down all at once, is that not a grievous error?

sentences.zh: 在禮太子朝夕視膳，昏定晨省，跪問安否，於情得盡。

translations.literal: At ritual crown prince morning-evening inspect meals, dusk settle dawn inquire, kneel ask peace-or-not, at affection attain exhaust.
translations.idiomatic: By ritual the crown prince attends his parents' meals morning and evening, secures them at night and greets them at dawn, and kneels to ask after their health, whereby affection finds full expression.

sentences.zh: 五日一朝，于敬既簡，於恩亦疏，易致構間。

translations.literal: Five-days one court-audience, at reverence already curtailed, at grace also distant, easy cause sow-estrangement.
translations.idiomatic: Audience once every five days makes reverence perfunctory and affection remote, and readily breeds estrangement and intrigue.

sentences.zh: 故曰「一朝不朝，其間容刀」。

translations.literal: Therefore say one court-audience not court-audience, between-it permits knife.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: "Miss one audience, and a knife may slip between them."

sentences.zh: 五日之制，起漢高祖，身為天子，父為庶人，萬機事多，故闕私敬耳。

translations.literal: Five-days regulation, rise Han Gaozu, body as Son-of-Heaven, father as commoner, myriad pivots affairs many, therefore lack private reverence ear.
translations.idiomatic: The five-day rule began with Han Gaozu: he was Son of Heaven while his father remained a commoner, myriad state affairs pressed, so private observances were curtailed.

sentences.zh: 今主上臨朝，太子無事，專主孝養，宜改此俗。

translations.literal: Now lord-above attend court, crown prince no affairs, solely master filial nurture, fitting change this vulgar-custom.
translations.idiomatic: Now Our Lord holds court while the crown prince has no competing duties and should devote himself wholly to filial care; this custom ought to be reformed.

sentences.zh: 《文王世子》篇曰：「王季一飯亦一飯，再飯亦再飯。

translations.literal: "King-Wen Heir" chapter says: Wang Ji one meal also one meal, second meal also second meal.
translations.idiomatic: The "Heir of King Wen" chapter says: "When Wang Ji ate once, he ate once; when he ate twice, he ate twice."

sentences.zh: 」安有逸豫五日一覲哉！

translations.literal: How have leisure ease five-days one visit!
translations.idiomatic: How could there be leisure to visit only once every five days?

sentences.zh: 纘又陳：

translations.literal: Zuan again set-forth:
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zuan further argued:

sentences.zh: 今迎太子神柩，孤魂獨行，太孫幼沖，不可涉道。

translations.literal: Now welcome crown-prince spirit-coffin, lone soul alone travel, imperial-great-grandson young tender, not can tread road.
translations.idiomatic: In welcoming the crown prince's catafalque, his orphaned spirit travels alone; the imperial great-grandson is too young to risk the journey.

sentences.zh: 謂可遣妃奉迎遠路，令其父衍隨行衛護。

translations.literal: Say can dispatch consort welcome-go distant road, order her father Yan follow-go guard-protect.
translations.idiomatic: I propose sending the consort to escort him from afar and ordering her father Yan to accompany the party and guard him.

sentences.zh: 皇太子初見誣陷，臣家門無祐，三世假親，具嘗辛苦，以家觀國，固知太子有變。

translations.literal: Imperial crown-prince first see slander-trap, your subject family-gate no blessing, three generations nominal kin, all taste hardship-bitter, take family view state, firmly know crown-prince have crisis.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was first framed, my house lacked fortune; for three generations we were nominal imperial kin and tasted every hardship; viewing the realm through my family, I knew the heir faced disaster.

sentences.zh: 臣故求副監國，欲依邴吉故事，距違來使，供養擁護，身親飲食醫藥，冀足救危。

translations.literal: Your subject therefore sought deputy oversee-realm, wish according-to Bing Ji old precedent, reject oppose come envoy, supply nurture embrace shield, body personally drink-food medicine drugs, hope sufficient save peril.
translations.idiomatic: Hence I sought appointment as deputy regent, wishing to follow Bing Ji's precedent: turning back the arriving envoys, supplying and sheltering him, and personally tending food and medicine, hoping thereby to stave off catastrophe.

sentences.zh: 主者以臣名資輕淺，不肯見與。

translations.literal: Those-in-charge take your subject name standing light shallow, not willing see grant.
translations.idiomatic: Those in charge deemed my name and standing too slight and refused to grant it.

sentences.zh: 世人見笑，謂為此職進退難居，有必死憂。

translations.literal: World men see laugh, say take this office advance-retreat hard abide, have certain-death worry.
translations.idiomatic: The world mocked it, saying this post left one nowhere between advance and retreat and carried the certainty of death.

sentences.zh: 臣獨以為苟全儲君，賈氏所誅，甘心所願。

translations.literal: Your subject alone take-as if preserve heir-apparent, Jia clan what execute, sweet-heart what wish.
translations.idiomatic: I alone thought that if the heir could be kept safe, execution by the Jia clan would be my willing choice.

sentences.zh: 今監國御史直副皆當三族，侍衛無狀，實自宜然。

translations.literal: Now oversee-realm censor straight deputy all merit three clans, attendant-guards no-form, solid self fitting thus.
translations.idiomatic: Now the regent's censors, deputies, and attendants all merit extermination of three clans; the guards behaved disgracefully and plainly deserved it.

sentences.zh: 臣謂其小人，不足具責。

translations.literal: Your subject call them petty men, not sufficient fully blame.
translations.idiomatic: I regard them as petty men unworthy of exhaustive blame.

sentences.zh: 故孔子曰：「可以托六尺之孤，臨大節而不可奪。

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius say can entrust six-foot orphan, face great integrity yet not can seize-away.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Confucius said: "One may entrust him with a six-foot orphan; faced with great crisis he cannot be swayed."

sentences.zh: 」是以聖王慎選。

translations.literal: Therefore sage king careful select.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the sage king chooses with care.

sentences.zh: 故河南尹向雄，昔能犯難葬故將鐘會，文帝嘉之，始拔顯用，至於先帝，以為右率。

translations.literal: Therefore Henan Governor Xiang Xiong, formerly able brave-difficulty bury former commander Zhong Hui, Wendi praise him, first pull conspicuous employ, reach late-emperor, take-as Right Leader.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Metropolitan Governor Xiang Xiong of Henan, who once braved danger to bury his former commander Zhong Hui, won praise from King Wen and was first raised to conspicuous office; under the late emperor he became Right Leader of the Household Guards.

sentences.zh: 如間之事，若得向雄之比，則豈可觸哉！

translations.literal: Like interval matters, if obtain Xiang Xiong compare-sort, then how can strike!
translations.idiomatic: In such a crisis, had men comparable to Xiang Xiong been found, how could disaster have struck?

sentences.zh: 此二使者，但為愚怯，亦非與謀，但可誅身，自全三族。

translations.literal: These two envoys, only be foolish cowardly, also not join plot, only can punish body, self preserve three clans.
translations.idiomatic: These two envoys were merely foolish and timid and were not party to the plot; executing them alone would suffice and spare their three clans.

sentences.zh: 如郭俶、郭斌，則于刑為當。

translations.literal: Like Guo Xu Guo Bin, then at punishment as fitting.
translations.idiomatic: As for Guo Xu and Guo Bin, capital punishment would be appropriate.

sentences.zh: 又東宮亦宜妙選忠直亮正，如向雄比。

translations.literal: Also Eastern Palace also fitting subtle-select loyal straight bright upright, like Xiang Xiong compare.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace likewise ought to be staffed through careful selection of loyal, frank, and upright men comparable to Xiang Xiong.

sentences.zh: 陛下千秋萬歲之後，太孫幼沖，選置兵衛，宜得柱石之士如周昌者。

translations.literal: Your Majesty thousand-autumns myriad-years after, imperial-great-grandson young tender, select place troops guards, fitting obtain pillar-stone gentlemen like Zhou Chang persons.
translations.idiomatic: After Your Majesty's passing, the imperial great-grandson will still be a child; in choosing palace guards you should obtain pillar-like stalwarts such as Zhou Chang of Han.

sentences.zh: 世俗淺薄，士無廉節，賈謐小兒，恃寵恣睢，而淺中弱植之徒，更相翕習，故世號魯公二十四友。

translations.literal: World custom shallow thin, gentlemen lack integrity honor, Jia Mi young boy, rely favor reckless stare, yet shallow-inside weak-root sort persons, mutually inhale practice, therefore age style Duke-Lu twenty-four friends.
translations.idiomatic: Custom is shallow and gentlemen lack integrity; Jia Mi the stripling, trusting in favor, indulges his whims, while hollow mediocrities flock together by imitation, hence the age styles them the Twenty-four Friends of Duke Lu.

sentences.zh: 又謐前見臣表理太子，曰：「閻兒作此為健，然觀其意，欲與諸司馬家同。

translations.literal: Also Mi formerly see your subject memorial straighten crown-prince, say Yan boy do this as stalwart, yet observe his intent, wish with various Sima houses same.
translations.idiomatic: When Mi earlier saw my memorial vindicating the crown prince, he said: "That Yan boy has shown nerve; still, judging his purpose, he means to side with the Sima houses."

sentences.zh: 」皆為臣寒心。

translations.literal: All for your subject chill heart.
translations.idiomatic: All of this struck dread into my heart.

sentences.zh: 伏見詔書，稱明滿奮、樂廣。

translations.literal: Prostrate see edict document, praise-display Man Fen Yue Guang.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen the edict that singles out Man Fen and Yue Guang for praise.

sentences.zh: 侍郎賈胤，與謐親理，而亦疏遠，往免父喪之後，停家五年，雖為小屈，有識貴之。

translations.literal: Gentleman-attendant Jia Yin, with Mi kin pattern, yet also distant-aloof, formerly finish father mourning after, stop home five years, although as small bend, have insight esteem him.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman-attendant Jia Yin is kin to Mi yet keeps his distance; after completing mourning for his father he remained at home five years. Though a modest humiliation, discerning men honored him for it.

sentences.zh: 潘岳、繆征等皆謐父党，共相沈浮，人士羞之，聞其晏然，莫不為怪。

translations.literal: Pan Yue Miao Zheng etc. all Mi father faction, mutually sink-float, gentlemen shame them, hear their peaceful calm, none not as strange.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Yue, Miao Zheng, and their like belonged to Mi's father's clique and rose and fell together; gentlemen were ashamed of them, and hearing they remained unruffled, everyone found it odd.

sentences.zh: 今詔書暴揚其罪，並皆遣出，百姓咸雲清當，臣獨謂非。

translations.literal: Now edict document violent-display their crimes, together all dispatch-out, hundred surnames all say clear right, your subject alone say not.
translations.idiomatic: Now the edict publicly airs their offenses and banishes them all; the common folk call it just, but I alone disagree.

sentences.zh: 但嶽征二十四人，宜皆齊黜，以肅風教。

translations.literal: Only Yue Zheng twenty-four persons, fitting all alike dismiss, thereby rectify wind teaching.
